papers.title: A Fix for Softmax and Cross-Entropy
papers.abstract: Standard implementations of softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy have two numerical bugs. The first bug, Softmax Collapse, rounds the target logit's gradient to zero if that one logit is much larger than the others, resulting in gradients that no longer sum to zero. The second bug, Softmax Cancellation, occurs when student logits are close to teacher logits, and produces non-zero gradients even when the student and teacher logits are equal. We present simple implementations of log-softmax, softmax, and cross-entropy that fix both bugs. Our fix eliminates the previously observed "slingshot" phenomenon, speeds up grokking with weight decay, prevents accuracy collapse without weight decay, stops student networks from drifting away from the teacher during distillation, and shows that after memorization, logit growth is bounded by an equilibrium between weight decay and Adam's $\epsilon$ hyperparameter.
papers.feed_description: Numerically stable softmax and cross-entropy preserve accurate gradients at extreme confidence, preventing training spikes and spurious drift during distillation.

paper_summary.summary: Authors rewrite softmax, log-softmax, and cross-entropy to preserve gradients lost at high confidence or when student and teacher outputs nearly match, addressing Softmax Collapse and Softmax Cancellation without higher-precision casting. In an fp32 grokking experiment, test accuracy fell from 61% to 23% with standard cross-entropy, while fixed cross-entropy reached 85%; these results are specific, and studied extremes are uncommon in large-scale training.
paper_summary.feedDescription: Numerically stable softmax and cross-entropy preserve accurate gradients at extreme confidence, preventing training spikes and spurious drift during distillation.

papers.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
papers.abstract: Frontier LLMs can read raw neural network weights to tell what a network does, and write or edit weights directly to fix or build networks without gradient descent.
papers.feed_description: The post demonstrates that a general-purpose language model can inspect network weights to infer behaviors and directly edit them to fix specific failures.

paper_summary.summary: The authors show that GPT-6 Astra, a general-purpose frontier LLM, can read and write neural network weights directly, without gradient descent or trained helper models. Across eight experiments it identifies what small networks were trained on from their weights, fixes and writes game-playing policies, and edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights to stop reasoning loops. They call this Weight-Space Programming.
originalProblem: Neural network weights are written by optimizers like Adam, by networks trained to generate weights, or by compilers from formal programs; humans cannot read or handcraft them.
LLM-driven optimization has been limited to text artifacts such as prompts, harnesses, and training code, on the assumption that weights can't be optimized by reasoning.
Prior LLM interpretability work relies on models trained specifically to read activations or weights, or on explaining single neurons.
solution: Give a general-purpose LLM a network's raw weights as text, or a Python sandbox over them for larger models, plus a natural-language goal.
Ask it to read the weights (what game, shape, language or behavior), fix a failure by editing weights, or write a network from scratch.
Allow no training loops, gradients, or search; in some experiments a small budget of forward passes lets it test its edits.
keyInsights: Astra reads structure directly: it named the game for all four PPO policies and found every induction head in transformers stripped of their input and output layers.
It writes networks as programs, e.g. a Breakout layer that computes where the ball will land and a Go network built from liberty and group-danger features.
Weight edits can remove an obstacle that hides an ability, like Qwen's looping, but could not add math ability to Gemma 3 270M, which rarely loops.
From weights alone it could not identify a sycophantic Gemma 3 270M; with attention patterns on its own probe texts it picked the sycophant in all three pairs.
results: One-shot MinAtar networks written with no training beat PPO trained for 100M steps in all three games, scoring 517.4 vs 25.3 for 500M-step PPO in Breakout.
A one-shot edit of 3.5% of a Kinetix car policy's weights raised success from 0% to 100% over 1,024 episodes.
A from-scratch 1.5M-weight Go network beat an equal-sized PPO network trained on 20 million games, given 50 forward passes.
Editing 131,072 of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights raised MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%, GSM8K from 13.8% to 67.1%, and IFEval from 21.0% to 62.3%.

papers.title: Proving and Improving the Platonic Representation Hypothesis with JEPAs
papers.abstract: Whether models trained on different modalities converge to the same representation of the world is central to AI. The Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH) conjectures that they do as they scale, but without a proof it offers neither a guarantee nor a recipe. We turn the hypothesis into a theorem. First, we prove a \emph{Platonic Representation Theorem}: Joint-Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) trained separately on any number of modalities learn the same representation up to one rotation whenever their positive pairs are two observations of one scene--\emph{good views}--and their misalignment is bounded otherwise. Second, we show that next-token prediction is a JEPA with \emph{bad views}, parts of a single document, which explains why language models align with vision only through scale. Third, we validate the theory from 145k captions to the texts of 940M web images, and uncover a scaling law of alignment that predicts unseen runs within seed noise. Good views need 42 times fewer training samples than next-token prediction on the same corpus to reach the same alignment, and a 109M-parameter text JEPA aligns with DINOv2 and CLIP's image encoders better than every language model we evaluated, up to 72B parameters, and than CLIP's text encoder: next-token prediction is a remarkably inefficient route to platonic representations. As a showcase, one rotation turns separately trained encoders into an image captioner (CIDEr .838 on COCO). Even that rotation needs no pair: on the latest pair-free benchmark, our text JEPA beats every zero-shot accuracy reported with language models up to 8B parameters, e.g., 64\% against at most 56\% top-5 on ImageNet-100. Positive views, and not scale alone, are thus the lever to build platonic representations.
papers.feed_description: Training models on multiple descriptions of the same scene can make their independently learned representations align, offering a more data-efficient alternative to next-token prediction.

paper_summary.summary: The authors test whether positive views can align separately trained text and image representations. A JEPA trained on different descriptions of the same scene learns stronger alignment than one trained on corruptions of a single description. On WIT-1024, the 109M-parameter model scores .184 against DINOv2 ViT-B, exceeding Qwen2.5-72B’s .154; the theorem’s idealized assumptions limit generalization.
paper_summary.feedDescription: Training models on multiple descriptions of the same scene can make their independently learned representations align, offering a more data-efficient alternative to next-token prediction.
originalProblem: The Platonic Representation Hypothesis proposes that models trained on different modalities may learn similar representations, but gives limited guidance on when this happens or how to encourage it.
Conventional self-supervised positives—such as augmented views of one image or a text prefix and continuation—can preserve observation-specific details that do not match across modalities.
It is unclear whether better-defined shared-scene examples can improve alignment more efficiently than simply scaling language-model training.
solution: The authors analyze JEPAs through the structure of their positive pairs, distinguishing good views of a shared world state from corruptions of the same observation that may retain modality-specific nuisance information.

They prove that, under finite-world, injective-rendering, and objective-identifiability assumptions, JEPAs with the same positive-pair distribution learn equivalent embeddings up to rotation; they also bound mismatch when the pair distributions differ.

Experiments compare text JEPAs, masked-span models, and next-token models against independently trained image encoders, evaluating neighborhood overlap, CKA, retrieval, captioning, and pair-free alignment.
keyInsights: Alignment depends not only on model scale but on which underlying states the training objective treats as related; shared positive-pair structure can make independently learned embeddings compatible.

Positive pairs that connect separate observations of the same scene encourage representations of shared content, while pairs that preserve nuisance details can consume embedding dimensions and limit cross-modal alignment.

Next-token prediction can be interpreted as having a JEPA-like positive relation between prefixes and continuations, but this does not explicitly group text by shared scenes; the analogy does not make the theoretical results directly applicable to language models.
results: On Flickr30k, rotation-based image-to-caption retrieval reached 4.4% rank-one accuracy for the good-view JEPA, versus 2.7% for masked-span training and 2.1% for next-token prediction; chance was 0.1%.

On WIT-1024, the 109M-parameter good-view JEPA scored 0.184 in mutual 10-nearest-neighbor alignment with DINOv2 ViT-B, compared with 0.154 for Qwen2.5-72B, 0.111 for a same-data next-token control, and 0.088 for a bad-view control. In one sample-efficiency comparison, it matched next-token alignment using 21.6M samples instead of 900M.

Applications include a captioning system with CIDEr 0.838, where only the map between independently trained encoders uses paired image-caption data, and pair-free ImageNet-100 alignment reaching 64.4% top-five accuracy. These findings are subject to idealized theory assumptions and experimental limits, including the use of recaptions generated by a vision-language model.

papers.title: SuperMimic: Scaling Humanoid Whole-Body Control with One Differentiable World Model
papers.abstract: Tracking large human-motion datasets has become the dominant route to general, expressive humanoid whole-body control, but scaling across many motions is expensive. Current pipelines use model-free reinforcement learning, either merging per-motion specialists through lossy distillation, or brute-forcing a single policy with cluster-scale compute. SuperMimic amortizes learning across all motions with one differentiable world model of their shared dynamics, fit from logged transitions of a standard rigid-body simulator. The world model and the tracking policy train together in one loop, and backpropagation-through-time over short imagined rollouts gives the policy analytic gradients. Fast imagined rollouts and analytic gradients make policy learning efficient. In 3 hours on a single GPU, SuperMimic surpasses the return of a state-of-the-art motion tracker baseline trained for 7 days on 128 GPUs. It reduces GPU-hours by more than $1000\times$ and fails on only 25 of 129,514 benchmark motions, versus 179 failures for the baseline. After 9.8 hours on two GPUs, SuperMimic achieves zero failures. From 1 to 264 hours of motion, the world model's prediction error stays stable, and GPU-hours to a target return grow slowly. Our policy transfers to a physical Unitree G1 across diverse and acrobatic motions. SuperMimic removes compute as the bottleneck to scaling humanoid whole-body control, making it practical to measure motion-tracking scaling laws.
papers.feed_description: A learned dynamics model lets a humanoid controller match large motion libraries with over 1,000 times fewer GPU-hours than cluster-scale training.

paper_summary.summary: SuperMimic trains a humanoid controller to track reference motions by learning shared dynamics in a differentiable world model and improving its policy through imagined rollouts. On the 129,514-motion BONES-SEED training benchmark, it exceeds SONIC’s released-checkpoint normalized return after 3 hours on one H100, with 25 failures versus 179 under differing failure criteria; the comparison is not hardware- or data-matched.
paper_summary.feedDescription: A learned dynamics model lets a humanoid controller match large motion libraries with over 1,000 times fewer GPU-hours than cluster-scale training.
originalProblem: Training whole-body controllers across large motion libraries can require extensive simulator rollouts and substantial multi-GPU compute.
Policies for different motions operate the same robot, but model-free training does not directly reuse that shared dynamics structure to reduce policy-learning cost.
Differentiating through contact-rich simulators can be difficult, limiting direct gradient-based optimization of motion-tracking policies.
solution: Learn a single dynamics world model from transitions collected in MuJoCo Warp, predicting future states and rewards while conditioning on randomized simulator properties.
Optimize the policy by backpropagating through 32-step imagined trajectories, with a critic estimating returns beyond the rollout horizon.
Train the model and policy in an alternating loop, so the learned model can be used even when the underlying simulator does not provide gradients.
keyInsights: A world model learned from simulator data can provide useful policy gradients without differentiating through the simulator itself.
The learned model’s short-horizon prediction error remains in the reported 0.007–0.011 range as the motion dataset grows from 1 to 264 hours.

Both faster imagined rollouts and gradient-based updates contribute to efficiency: rollouts are over 10× faster than MuJoCo Warp at practical batch sizes, and the method uses about 64× fewer imagined steps than PPO on model rollouts to reach its best training return.
results: On a shared benchmark of 129,514 training motions, SuperMimic exceeds the released SONIC checkpoint after three hours on one H100 and has zero failed motions after 9.8 hours on two H100s; the authors estimate over 1,000× lower training compute than SONIC, with hardware and dataset differences limiting the comparison.
On 40 LAFAN1 clips, SuperMimic reaches an evaluation return of 0.82 in 1.2 hours on one GPU, while PPO does not reach that target within 18 hours and ends at 0.60 on one GPU or 0.72 on eight.

The authors demonstrate selected motions on a physical Unitree G1 without per-motion tuning. In an exploratory velocity-command study, the learned encoder has lower steady-state error on 650 of 672 commands, though each policy uses only one training seed.

papers.title: Agentic World Action Models
papers.abstract: Recent world action models provide visual foresight and future prediction for robot manipulation, but lack explicit mechanisms for compositional skill reuse. Agentic robotics combines code-based planning and reasoning with reusable skills, but often lacks predictive grounding in physical dynamics. We introduce AW-0, an agentic world action model framework that integrates code-based planning with joint video and action prediction. We jointly model code, future video, and robot actions as three coupled generative streams within a unified mixture-of-transformers architecture. Within this architecture a code expert generates parameterized skill routines and control logic while video and action experts generate future visual states and low-level motor commands. Code serves two complementary roles: it structures multi-step prediction and control within the world model and represents skills as reusable programs for subsequent agentic execution. We further introduce an automated curation pipeline that labels robot and human video trajectories with aligned programs and consolidates recurring routines into reusable skill libraries. Evaluations on RoboTwin 2.0 and physical bimanual manipulation tasks show improved task performance over VLA and WAM baselines, alongside gains in language following, semantic reasoning and robustness, demonstrating that agentic code enables connection between planning, prediction and execution within WAMs.
papers.feed_description: Combining reusable code-based skill plans with visual foresight helps robots perform complex manipulation across parallel-gripper and dexterous-hand tasks.

paper_summary.summary: AW-0 adds a skill-program stream to a model that predicts future video and actions for language-directed manipulation. The program can guide imagined states and action generation, but is usually a plan conditioning an action expert rather than executable code. Across eight bimanual tasks, AW-0 scores 71.1% on average versus DreamZero’s 46.0%; rubric scores measure partial-credit progress, not full task success.
paper_summary.feedDescription: Combining reusable code-based skill plans with visual foresight helps robots perform complex manipulation across parallel-gripper and dexterous-hand tasks.

papers.title: The Exponential Time Hypothesis Is False
papers.abstract: We give a deterministic algorithm for exactly counting the satisfying assignments of an arbitrary k-CNF formula. For every fixed k ⩾ 2, on a formula with n variables and m clauses, our algorithm uses poly_k(n, m) space and runs in time (n + m)^{O_k(1)} 2^{n/(log n)^{1/2 + o(1)}}. Our algorithm refutes the Exponential Time Hypothesis (ETH), which postulates that deciding 3-SAT on n variables requires 2^{Ω(n)} time in the worst case.
papers.feed_description: A deterministic subexponential-time algorithm exactly counts satisfying assignments for every fixed-width CNF, overturning a foundational assumption about worst-case 3-SAT.

paper_summary.summary: The authors give a deterministic algorithm for exactly counting satisfying assignments of Boolean formulas with fixed-width clauses. It reorganizes assignment sums into group-by-group sums using shared measurements and interpolation. For each fixed width, the worst-case running time is polynomial in the input size times 2^{O(n log log n/√log n)}, with polynomial space; the exponent improves for linearly many clauses, but this does not give subexponential algorithms for general NP problems.
paper_summary.feedDescription: A deterministic subexponential-time algorithm exactly counts satisfying assignments for every fixed-width CNF, overturning a foundational assumption about worst-case 3-SAT.
originalProblem: ETH and related hypotheses posit that fixed-width SAT cannot be solved in subexponential time, underpinning conditional lower bounds for many problems.
Exact counting is harder to decompose than decision: constraints share variables, coupling the global sum over assignments and limiting prior counting algorithms to exponential time.
The goal is to obtain subexponential exact counting without introducing enough auxiliary variables to erase the runtime savings.
solution: The method encodes satisfying assignments algebraically, deforms variable inputs using a parameter, and uses Hermite interpolation to recover the desired count from efficiently evaluated polynomial data.
At selected evaluation points, interactions between variable groups are summarized by a small set of bounded integer measurements, allowing assignment sums to be computed groupwise.
For general formulas, the framework is combined with sparsification or sparse polynomial-system encodings; a tensor-contraction refinement yields the sharpest stated bound.
keyInsights: A global counting problem can become separable when cross-group dependence is routed through a controlled set of shared measurements.
Interpolation can recover the original count from transformed instances, while computing Taylor coefficients at evaluation points helps limit the number of evaluations required.
The authors claim the approach extends beyond SAT counting to several other exact-counting and optimization tasks, though these consequences depend on the central proof being correct.
results: For fixed clause width \(k\), the claimed deterministic exact-counting runtime is \((n+m)^{O_k(1)}2^{O_k(n\log\log n/\sqrt{\log n})}\); for bounded-density formulas it improves to \((n+m)^{O_{k,D}(1)}2^{O_{k,D}(n/\sqrt{\log n})}\). Both are subexponential in the number of variables.

The authors infer that SAT decision and exact counting are in deterministic subexponential time for every fixed width, contradicting ETH, SETH, #ETH, and several related hypotheses if the theorem holds.

Reported applications include finding satisfying assignments, uniform sampling, additive approximation for Max-\(k\)-SAT, and subexponential algorithms for counting independent sets, proper colorings, and perfect matchings.

papers.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
papers.abstract: We introduce an approach for self-supervised representation learning designed to be used as a tokenizer for generative modeling. Our objective supervises a representation loss by factorizing the pointwise mutual information of the data, which we estimate by taking information differences between conditional predictions from a learned generative model. We justify our algorithm theoretically and empirically, demonstrating that our generative approach to representation learning avoids dimensional collapse and feature suppression in cases where commonly used methods like DINO and LeJEPA fail. Moreover, we show our representation learning technique is scalable; expending more compute leads to predictably better latent tokenization. For the first time, we perform a careful analysis of the combined flop efficiency of tokenizer and generative model and demonstrate that our approach is a compute-optimal improvement over direct diffusion for pixel-space generation, obtaining an FID-50K of 2.18 with JiT-L. Applied to ImageNet and the text-to-image dataset GPIC, we show tokenizer encoder scaling laws for diffusability, where extrapolating our approach achieves representations in 7x fewer FLOPs than DINOv2 on ImageNet and 8x fewer FLOPs than WebSSL on GPIC.
papers.feed_description: Learning visual tokenizers alongside image generators can improve image generation at equal training compute compared with generating directly from pixels.

paper_summary.summary: RePR trains image representations to capture how context improves a generative predictor’s predictions of image patches. It uses this signal to guide a tokenizer, then generates pixels from that representation. On ImageNet, 50,000 generations yield FID 2.18 for RePR-78M plus JiT-L versus 2.36 for pixel JiT-L at nearly matched training compute. This compares training FLOPs, not inference cost.
paper_summary.feedDescription: Learning visual tokenizers alongside image generators can improve image generation at equal training compute compared with generating directly from pixels.
originalProblem: Representation encoders trained for recognition may suppress image details that matter for generation, making their features less suitable as generative tokens.
Features used by a generator are not always directly supervised during encoder training, and existing tokenizer approaches can impose compression or optimization constraints.
It is unclear when spending compute on representation learning improves generation enough to offset the encoder’s training cost.
solution: The method, RePR, trains patch-level representations to match pointwise mutual information estimates between image views, derived from conditional likelihood comparisons with a generative prediction model.
It weights information across corruption scales and estimates whole-image dependencies through incremental, patch-by-patch targets to make training more tractable.
The authors evaluate representation scaling and generation under compute-matched budgets, including experiments with iterative feature prediction and a latent-generation setup.
keyInsights: Generative likelihood-based supervision offers an alternative to contrastive objectives and may reduce feature suppression; in a watermark stress test, RePR retained class-probing performance better than LeJEPA and DINOv3.
Across tested compute ranges on ImageNet and GPIC, larger or more extensively trained RePR encoders generally improved generation, with reported power-law scaling trends.
Representation training can be worthwhile when its cost is counted: the reported RePR system used nearly the same total FLOPs as pixel-space JiT-L while attaining a lower FID-50K.
results: On ImageNet, RePR-78M with pixel JiT-L trained for 440 epochs used 3.49 × 10²⁰ FLOPs and achieved FID-50K 2.18; pixel-space JiT-L at 600 epochs used 3.57 × 10²⁰ FLOPs and achieved 2.36.

Scaling trends led the authors to extrapolate that RePR could reach DINOv2-level ImageNet performance with roughly 7–8× fewer encoder-training FLOPs, and WebSSL-level GPIC performance with roughly 8× fewer; these estimates were not directly tested at the extrapolated budgets.
In a separate GAN-and-perceptual-loss decoder comparison, third-iteration RePR achieved FID-50K 11.13 after 20 epochs of DiT-XL training, versus 12.46 for I-JEPA-H and 13.84 for MoCo v3.

papers.title: Are We Overthinking One-Step Generation?
papers.abstract: Diffusion and flow matching are now dominant frameworks for generative modeling in continuous domains, but they typically require multiple network evaluations at inference. This has motivated extensive research on one-step generative modeling primarily built on diffusion and flow, though existing approaches often rely on complex training machinery. In this work, we introduce Priming Models, a simple two-stage framework for training one-step generators. Motivated by the difficulty of distributional training from scratch, Priming Models are first trained on a reconstruction objective, e.g., pixel-space denoising at a fixed noise level, before undergoing feature-space distributional post-training. Our central scientific finding is that this simple reconstruction stage is already enough to entirely alleviate the difficulty of distributional training. Empirically, across class-conditional image generation, text-to-image generation, and world modeling, Priming Models significantly advance the Pareto frontier of training compute vs. generation quality. On ImageNet at $256 \times 256$ resolution, we achieve a state-of-the-art FID of $1.19$ among one-step generators using approximately one-tenth the training compute of prior methods with comparable FID. We open-source our codebase at this https URL.
papers.feed_description: Reconstruction pretraining lets generators learn high-quality one-step image synthesis through simpler distributional training, without relying on a pretrained diffusion model.

paper_summary.summary: Priming Models train a one-step image generator by first reconstructing clean images from corrupted inputs, then matching generated and real examples in frozen feature space. On ImageNet, Priming-L reaches FID 1.19 in one network pass using 238.95 EFLOPs, versus Drifting-L’s FID 1.61 using 1,476.39 EFLOPs. This is about 6.2 times less reported training compute for this comparison only.
paper_summary.feedDescription: Reconstruction pretraining lets generators learn high-quality one-step image synthesis through simpler distributional training, without relying on a pretrained diffusion model.
originalProblem: One-step generators can reduce sampling latency, but direct distribution-matching training can be difficult and computationally expensive, especially from random initialization.
Many fast-generation methods rely on pretrained diffusion or flow teachers, trajectory supervision, or specialized optimization procedures.
It is unclear whether a simpler preparatory task can make direct one-step distribution learning effective across different generative settings.
solution: Pretrain the same network to reconstruct clean data from Gaussian-corrupted inputs, using a fixed high noise level and, for ImageNet, perceptual feature losses.

Use the pretrained network directly as a one-step generator, then post-train it with entropy-regularized optimal transport in frozen feature spaces, including a repulsive term to discourage sample collapse.
Evaluate the recipe on class-conditional ImageNet, text-to-image generation, and action-conditioned future-frame prediction for robot manipulation.
keyInsights: Reconstruction pretraining is a preparation for distributional refinement, not the final generative objective: high-quality samples emerge during post-training.
The amount of retained signal in the corrupted input matters; ImageNet results were strongest at noise level 0.8, while fully noisy inputs performed poorly.

The authors’ Jacobian-alignment analysis is consistent with the idea that pretraining helps the model respond to distributional correction directions, though it does not establish this as the sole cause.
results: On ImageNet-1K at 256 × 256, the Large model reports FID 1.19 and five-space Fréchet distance 7.10 at 238.95 EFLOPs, compared with reported FIDs of 1.61 for Drifting-L and 1.33 for W-Flow XL/2 at higher training compute.
For 512 × 512 text-to-image generation, a logit-normal pretraining variant reaches GenEval 0.818 and DPG-Bench 82.16; a two-step extension reaches 0.844 and 82.81, respectively.

In RT-1 and Bridge-V2 world modeling, Priming beats the one-step Drifting baseline on all reported metrics and uses less training compute; compared with 32-step flow matching, image metrics are generally better, although RT-1 FVD is higher.

papers.title: Training Foundation Models with a Single Algorithm
papers.abstract: Foundation models are typically trained in stages: pretraining, midtraining, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL), with changes in both data and learning algorithms. We show that this algorithmic separation is not fundamental. By deriving suitable RL objectives as maximum-likelihood fitting to model-generated target distributions, we place all of these stages under a single likelihood-based training algorithm, unified training. This perspective turns the foundation-model training lifecycle into a problem of choosing which data to train on, in what proportions, and when, with conventional staged training as a special case. We instantiate this framework in a unified training system that mixes static data and RL generations within a single trainer. Across controlled and real-world experiments, unified training improves the accuracy-compute tradeoff and task coverage while preserving broader capabilities, and provides a stronger starting point for continual learning. This work lays the groundwork for a unified science of foundation-model training, connecting mathematical principles, training infrastructure, and the development of model capabilities.

papers.title: RoboJEPA: Scaling Robotic Latent World Models
papers.abstract: Latent world models have shown a remarkable ability to predict future states and to plan in the real world. In practice, however, we lack a principled way to estimate how their capabilities scale with model size, data, and compute, an open problem that slows progress in the field. In this work we present RoboJEPA, a world model based on the Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA) and trained on a large-scale dataset spanning 12 robotic embodiments. We show that RoboJEPA's imagination error, the error of its latent rollouts, follows a second-order power law in compute, allowing us to predict model quality well beyond the scale at which the law is fit. We further show that downstream robotic planning performance improves predictably with compute, and that imagination error is strongly correlated with it, making it a reliable proxy for real-robot evaluation. Finally, we demonstrate that latent world models can be deployed zero-shot as robotic agents, planning toward a single goal image to solve tasks requiring long-horizon planning on real hardware. We release all model checkpoints together with our training and robot deployment code. To our knowledge, this is the first work to establish scaling laws for multi-embodiment robotic world models trained on real robot data, and RoboJEPA, at 8B parameters, is the largest JEPA predictor model trained to date.
papers.feed_description: Predictive scaling laws link robotic world-model accuracy to downstream planning, helping researchers estimate compute needs before costly real-robot evaluations.

paper_summary.summary: RoboJEPA predicts future visual features under robot actions and uses imagined outcomes to plan toward a goal image. Its predictor scales from 22 million to 8 billion parameters while keeping the V-JEPA 2.1 encoder fixed. A second-order compute law extrapolates held-out prediction error better than a standard power law, but does not establish a universal link to robot success.
paper_summary.feedDescription: Predictive scaling laws link robotic world-model accuracy to downstream planning, helping researchers estimate compute needs before costly real-robot evaluations.
originalProblem: Scaling laws are well studied for language and vision models, but less systematically measured for robotic world models trained on real robot data.
It is unclear whether lower offline prediction error reliably translates into better planning, or how much compute is needed for different robotic capabilities.
solution: Train action-conditioned transformer predictors over frozen V-JEPA 2.1 visual features using a mixture of 23 datasets, then measure latent rollout error across models from 22M to 8B parameters.
Fit compute-based scaling curves and evaluate image-goal planning with cross-entropy search in simulation and on a Franka robot.
keyInsights: A second-order power law forecasts held-out prediction error more accurately than a standard power law when extrapolating to 4B- and 8B-parameter models.
Planning capabilities appear at different compute scales: basic reaching comes first, followed by grasped-object transport, obstacle avoidance, and object pushing.
Longer-horizon tasks benefit from training with longer autoregressive rollouts, underscoring the importance of matching training to deployment demands.
results: Extrapolation error for the second-order law was 0.6 × 10⁻³ on DROID and 1.4 × 10⁻³ on RoboCasa, versus 2.0 × 10⁻³ and 3.7 × 10⁻³ for a standard power law.
In simulation, reaching emerged around 10²⁰ FLOPs, obstacle avoidance around 10²¹ FLOPs, and positive object-pushing success around 10²² FLOPs.
The 8B model achieved 67% success at grasping, 50% at lifting, and 27% at pick-and-place on the Franka robot.

papers.title: MiMo-V2.6: Scaling Reinforcement Learning Towards Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is the central training paradigm for advancing large foundation models towards self-improvement. This report introduces the MiMo-V2.6 series, an omni-modal family that pushes the frontier of model intelligence by scaling RL compute. Prior to RL, we conduct mid-training on a broad multimodal corpus to provide ample exploration space, and build a solid infrastructure on the pretrained hybrid-SWA architecture to support subsequent scale-up. We scale RL compute along three dimensions: (1) larger batches and higher throughput, with an asynchronous training that consumes 1,568 samples and 2.7-3.7B tokens per step at context lengths of up to 1M; (2) more diverse and complex environments, spanning code, general, visual, and cyber domains under a mixture of agent harnesses; and (3) more grader compute, via groupwise agentic grading that yields more accurate reward signals for long-horizon tasks and steers the model towards shorter, more token-efficient solutions. To keep training stable at scale, we freeze the MoE router and establish a multi-layer defense against reward hacking. We further build infrastructure for mixed-task agentic RL, including a unified trajectory representation, high-concurrency multi-framework rollout, decoupled control and data planes, and training-inference consistency. We open-source the training dynamics, RL environments, and RL framework to facilitate reproduction and further research on scaled RL and model self-improvement.
papers.feed_description: The report provides an open model, verified task environments, and training framework that researchers can use to test reinforcement learning across agent tasks.

paper_summary.summary: The authors train coding agents with groupwise grading, comparing attempts at the same task to add quality signals to binary test rewards. Online Groupwise Advantage Redistribution shifts positive credit toward higher-quality passing patches. MiMo-V2.6-Pro’s reported average pass-rate score across three sampled attempts rises from 58.4 to 72.6 on DeepSWE v1.1, but this mixed-task run does not isolate grading or compute effects.
paper_summary.feedDescription: The report provides an open model, verified task environments, and training framework that researchers can use to test reinforcement learning across agent tasks.
originalProblem: Agentic tasks involve long interaction sequences, multiple tools, and outcomes that are harder to verify than conventional coding tests, making reinforcement-learning feedback noisy and vulnerable to reward hacking.

Scaling RL across coding, workflows, visual tasks, and cybersecurity requires high-throughput infrastructure and stable training, while binary pass/fail rewards may fail to distinguish robust solutions from brittle workarounds.
solution: The authors pair multimodal MoE models with agent-focused mid-training and large-batch, asynchronous group-relative policy optimization across varied task environments and harnesses.

They add richer coding feedback through Groupwise Reward Synthesis and Groupwise Advantage Redistribution, alongside trajectory audits, reward-hacking defenses, router freezing, and infrastructure to align rollout and training behavior.
keyInsights: RL gains depend on the surrounding system—not only optimization scale—including task diversity, verifier quality, rollout throughput, and consistency between sampling and training.
Ranking successful solutions and redistributing learning advantage toward higher-quality ones helped sustain pass-rate gains while moderating rollout-length growth compared with training without GAR.
The results support iterative improvement through training on designed tasks, but do not establish that a model can autonomously redesign or improve its own training process.
results: On DeepSWE v1.1, average@3 rose from 58.4 to 72.6 for Pro and from 48.7 to 65.7 for Flash; on AutomationBench, Pro scored 53.1, ahead of the listed comparison models, while it scored 71.9 on DeepSWE versus 74.0 for Claude Opus 5.

Performance was uneven across evaluations: Pro reached 76.9 on Toolathlon-Verified, below the listed 80.6, and scored 17.8 on ExploitGym and 47.9 on ExploitBench, despite strong CyberGym scores of 94.0 for Pro and 95.1 for Flash.

The 9B distilled model improved on all 11 reported evaluations after domain-specific RL, including SWE-bench Verified (61.1 to 66.2) and Terminal Bench 2.1 (37.1 to 52.8); the largest-model runs reportedly cost $2.6 million for Pro and $0.9 million for Flash.

researcher.bio: Xiyu Wei co-authored Paperbanana, a system for automating academic illustration for AI scientists. Wei’s listed affiliation is Peking University, and their research focuses on LLMs. Their work also includes improving long-context language models with reasoning-path supervision and using rubrics to judge open-ended answers. They contributed to MiMo-V2.6, a large-collaboration project on scaling reinforcement learning toward self-improvement.

researcher.name: Xing Zhang
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Xiaomi Technology, Previously CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Xing Zhang works on programming languages and software engineering, with a focus on bidirectional transformations and live programming. They are a researcher at Xiaomi Technology. Their research includes methods that let programmers edit a program’s output and reflect those changes back into the source code. Zhang completed a PhD at Peking University in 2025 and earned a BEng from Nankai University. They also visited the University of Bristol’s Programming Languages Research Group in 2024.

researcher.name: Xin Zhang
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Fudan University
researcher.bio: Xin Zhang’s SpeechGPT gives LLMs intrinsic cross-modal conversational abilities. They are a CS PhD student at Fudan University whose research spans speech, multimodal LLMs, LLMs, and NLP. Their work also includes AnyGPT, which models multimodal data as discrete sequences, and SpeechTokenizer, a unified tokenizer for speech language models.

researcher.name: Xiaodong Ji
researcher.bio: Xiaodong Ji co-authored PqCache, which uses product quantization to reduce KV-cache costs in long-context LLM inference. Their listed affiliation is Peking University. Their work spans efficient LLM inference and RL post-training, including SALE, a low-bit estimator for sparse attention during long-context prefill. They also co-authored StaleFlow, which manages data staleness to mitigate skew in disaggregated RL post-training.

researcher.name: Wenhan Ma
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Wenhan Ma’s MiMo develops a training pipeline to scale reasoning in language models through integrated pretraining and posttraining. Ma is a CS PhD student at Peking University supervised by Professor Zhifang Sui, where they focus on RL for LLMs and training stability. Their research extends to multimodal and high-efficiency models through work on MiMo-VL and Mimo-v2-flash. In Stabilizing MoE Reinforcement Learning, Ma proposed aligning training and inference routers to improve the reliability of Mixture-of-Experts architectures. They also authored Mopd, a multi-teacher on-policy distillation method for integrating capabilities during LLM post-training. Ma earned a BA in Computer Science from Peking University before beginning their doctoral studies in 2025.

topAffiliation.description: Supervised by Professor Zhifang Sui; research focuses on reinforcement learning for large language models, particularly training stability.

researcher.name: Weimin Xiong
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Weimin Xiong co-developed Kimi k1.5, which scales reinforcement learning to improve the reasoning capabilities of LLMs. Xiong is a CS PhD student at Peking University, where they also earned their undergraduate degree. Their research focuses on LLM agents, RL, and automated planning. They contributed to Kimi k2 for open agentic intelligence and developed RestGPT to link LLMs with real-world applications using RESTful APIs. Additionally, Xiong created AgentBank for trajectory-based fine-tuning and authored Watch every step! to introduce iterative step-level refinement for agent learning. Their work also includes Mpo, which uses meta plan optimization to boost agent performance, and the Mimo-v2-flash technical report.

researcher.name: Shuhuai Ren
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Xiaomi MiMo, Previously Computer Science PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Video-mme, a benchmark for evaluating the long-form video analysis capabilities of multimodal LLMs, was co-created by Shuhuai Ren. He is a Research Scientist at Xiaomi MiMo and a PhD student at Peking University. Ren’s research centers on vision-language foundation models and unified architectures for multimodal understanding and generation. He developed the MiMo framework to increase the reasoning potential of LLMs through specialized training and introduced TimeChat to improve temporal sensitivity in long video processing. His earlier work in NLP proposed a probability-weighted word saliency method for generating natural language adversarial examples. Ren has held research internships at Microsoft Research Asia, ByteDance, and Amazon Web Services. He holds a BE from Huazhong University of Science and Technology.

researcher.name: Shuhao Gu
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Xiaomi, Previously Researcher @ BAAI
researcher.bio: Shuhao Gu co-authored MiMo-VL, a technical report detailing a vision-language model architecture. Gu is a researcher at Xiaomi focusing on LLMs, vision-language models, and AGI. They previously served as a researcher at BAAI and earned a PhD in NLP from the Chinese Academy of Sciences. Gu’s work on MiMo investigates methods for enhancing the reasoning potential of language models during both pretraining and posttraining. Other notable works include Infinity-mm, which scales multimodal performance with instruction data, and Mimo-v2-flash. Their earlier research addressed neural machine translation challenges, including document-level context modeling and domain adaptation.

researcher.name: Shijie Cao
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Xiaomi MiMo, Previously Senior Researcher, Systems @ Microsoft Research Asia
researcher.bio: Shijie Cao’s MiMo-v2-flash uses a Mixture-of-Experts architecture and hybrid attention to accelerate reasoning and agentic tasks. Cao is a researcher at Xiaomi MiMo and was previously a senior researcher in the Systems Group at Microsoft Research Asia. Their work focuses on software-hardware co-design for efficient LLM inference, specifically targeting low-bit quantization, sparse attention, and domain-specific architectures. They also developed T-mac, a kernel library for low-bit CPU deployment using lookup tables, and SeerAttention, which employs learnable gates to identify intrinsic attention sparsity. Cao earned a PhD in computer science from the Harbin Institute of Technology following a long-term research internship at Microsoft Research Asia. They serve as a program committee member for HPCA 2026.

researcher.name: Shaolei Zhang
researcher.affiliation: Assistant Professor, Renmin University of China
researcher.headline: Assistant Professor, Information @ Renmin University of China, Previously CS PhD Student @ Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
researcher.bio: Shaolei Zhang’s Llama-omni enables real-time speech interaction by equipping LLMs with simultaneous speech recognition and synthesis. Zhang is an Assistant Professor at the School of Information at Renmin University of China, where he collaborates with Ju Fan and Xiaoyong Du. His research focuses on multimodal LLMs and agentic systems, including LLaVA-Mini, which compresses image and video representations into a single vision token to increase efficiency. He also developed DeepAnalyze to automate the end-to-end data science pipeline using agentic LLMs. Zhang’s broader work covers hallucination mitigation via TruthX and simultaneous speech-to-speech translation with StreamSpeech. He earned a PhD from the Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and a BA from Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications.

topAffiliation.description: Collaborates closely with Professor Ju Fan and Professor Xiaoyong Du.

researcher.name: Rang Li
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Peking University, Previously CS BE Student @ Beijing Institute of Technology
researcher.bio: Rang Li’s MiMo-V2-Flash provides a technical framework for accelerating multimodal model performance. Li is a CS PhD student at Peking University advised by Prof. Zhifang Sui. Their research focuses on LLMs and vision-language learning, specifically regarding multimodal integration and agentic reliability. They also developed Mimo-audio to demonstrate few-shot learning capabilities in audio language models. Additionally, Li co-authored Claw-Eval to improve evaluation protocols for autonomous agents and GroundingME to evaluate visual grounding in multimodal models. They previously earned a BE in Computer Science through the Teli College Elite Program at the Beijing Institute of Technology.

topAffiliation.description: Advised by Prof. Zhifang Sui.

researcher.name: Minzheng Wang
researcher.affiliation: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Xiaomi MiMo, NLP PhD Student @ Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences
researcher.bio: Wang is a researcher at Xiaomi MiMo and a PhD student at the Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences. Their research focuses on LLMs and NLP, with specific emphasis on agentic RL and socially intelligent agents. Wang developed Adaptive Social Learning to optimize policies for language agents and co-authored MMEvol, which uses evolved instructions to train multimodal models. They previously held research internships at miHoYo and Alibaba Group and earned a BA in Automation from the Beijing Institute of Technology.

topAffiliation.description: Building Xiaomi MiMo, focusing on Harness and Agentic RL.

researcher.name: Liwen Wang
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ HKUST
researcher.bio: Liwen Wang’s MASLeak identifies intellectual property leakage vulnerabilities within multi-agent systems. A CS PhD student at HKUST, Wang focuses on LLM security and agentic architectures. They developed a watermarking method to protect the intellectual property of agentic systems and created CAM for causality-based analysis of multi-agent code generation. Wang also evaluates how multi-modal LLMs influence visual deep learning testing through image mutation. Their research further includes methods for testing and enhancing multi-agent systems to ensure robust code generation.

researcher.name: Linli Yao
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Peking University, Previously Information MSc Student @ Renmin University of China
researcher.bio: Linli Yao’s TimeChat applies time-sensitive modeling to MLLMs to improve long video understanding. Yao is a PhD student at Peking University’s School of Computer Science, where she researches multi-modal semantic understanding and efficient video processing. Her work on TimeChat-Online identifies visual token redundancy in streaming videos, while DeCo introduces a method for decoupling token compression from semantic abstraction. She has also developed the Generative Frame Sampler to optimize frame selection for video-language tasks. Before joining the Language Computing and Machine Learning Group at PKU, Yao earned her Master’s and Bachelor’s degrees from Renmin University of China. Her experience includes research internships at Kuaishou Technology, 01.AI, and Alibaba.

topAffiliation.description: Language Computing and Machine Learning Group (Lanco); supervised by Prof. Xu Sun.

researcher.name: Linghao Zhang
researcher.headline: Technical Staff @ Xiaomi MiMo, Previously Software Engineering BA Student @ Wuhan University
researcher.bio: Linghao Zhang co-developed SWE-bench to evaluate how LLMs resolve real-world software engineering tasks. Zhang is a member of the technical staff at Xiaomi MiMo, where they focus on RL, coding agents, and post-training. Their research centers on NLP and software engineering, including the development of DI-bench for benchmarking repository-scale dependency inference. They have also published work on commit message generation using RAG and LLMs. Prior to Xiaomi, Zhang was a research intern at Microsoft Research and completed a degree in software engineering at Wuhan University.

topAffiliation.description: Works on post-training, coding agents, and reinforcement learning.

researcher.name: Liang Zhao
researcher.affiliation: Xiaomi MiMo, SkyworkAI, Tencent, Alibaba, Peking University
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Xiaomi MiMo, Previously Researcher @ SkyworkAI
researcher.bio: Liang Zhao's MiMo develops a framework to improve the reasoning capabilities of language models throughout the pretraining and posttraining stages. Zhao is a researcher at Xiaomi MiMo and was previously a researcher at SkyworkAI, where they contributed to the Skywork foundation model series. Their research in LLMs and NLP also includes Mimo-v2-flash and work on mixture-of-experts training through Skywork-MoE. Zhao previously held research positions at Tencent and Alibaba DAMO Academy. They also co-developed KNAS, a gradient-independent method for neural architecture search. Zhao earned an MSc in Data Science from Peking University and a BA in Computer Science from Northwestern Polytechnical University.

topAffiliation.description: Contributed to the MiMo language-model project.

researcher.name: Lei Li
researcher.affiliation: University of Hong Kong, Peking University
researcher.headline: Core Contributor @ Xiaomi LLM-Core Team, PhD Student @ The University of Hong Kong
researcher.bio: Lei Li's A survey on in-context learning provides a framework for how LLMs perform tasks by processing example demonstrations within a prompt. He is a PhD student at the University of Hong Kong and a core contributor for the Xiaomi LLM-Core Team. His research centers on multimodal LLMs and vision-language learning, specifically regarding model alignment and benchmark development. Li created Video-mme to evaluate multimodal models on long-video analysis and led the development of the MiMo series of reasoning and vision-language models. His other notable works include Math-shepherd, a label-free verifier for mathematical reasoning, and the fairness assessment benchmark FairEval. He earned a master's degree from Peking University and has held research roles at Reka AI and Shanghai AI Lab.

topAffiliation.description: Contributed to MiMo V2.5, MiMo-V2-Omni, and MiMo-VL.

researcher.name: Jinhao Dong
researcher.headline: Lecturer @ Renmin University of China, Previously CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Jinhao Dong is a core contributor to MiMo, a report on developing reasoning-capable LMs from pretraining through post-training. They are a lecturer at Renmin University of China and a technical advisor to Xiaomi’s LLM Core Team, where they work on code-related LLM development, including pretraining and RL. Their research spans code generation, trustworthy software development, and SE methods augmented by AI. Earlier work includes FIRA, which represents code changes with fine-grained graphs to generate commit messages, and ConTested, which uses consistency checks for LLM code generation. Dong earned a PhD in computer science from Peking University and was a visiting scholar at the National University of Singapore.

topAffiliation.description: Joined the research group led by Professor Xiaoyong Du and Professor Wei Lu.

researcher.name: Jinyu Xiang
researcher.headline: Algorithm Researcher @ Xiaomi Mimo-Core, Previously Researcher @ DeepWisdom
researcher.bio: Jinyu Xiang’s Aflow optimizes agentic workflows by treating the design process as a search problem over code-represented sequences. They are an Algorithm Researcher at Xiaomi Mimo-Core, where they develop LLMs for reasoning, coding, and general agents. Xiang’s research on autonomous systems includes the OpenManus framework for building general agents and MiMo-Code, a CLI designed for the co-evolution of models and agents. They also co-authored a survey of self-evolving agents and developed self-supervised prompt optimization for iterative model refinement. Xiang previously worked at DeepWisdom and is an independent musician on Tencent Music.

topAffiliation.description: Works on large models for reasoning, coding, and agents.

researcher.name: Jianyu Wei
researcher.affiliation: Building MiMo. Previously USTC & MSRA Joint PhD
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ USTC-MSRA, Previously CS Student @ University of Science and Technology of China
researcher.bio: Jianyu Wei developed nn-Meter to predict deep-learning inference latency on edge devices using kernel-level performance modeling. Wei is a CS PhD student in the joint program between the University of Science and Technology of China and Microsoft Research Asia. Their research focuses on LLM infrastructure, RL infrastructure, and algorithm-system co-design for efficient model pretraining and deployment. Wei co-developed Pre-gated MoE to accelerate mixture-of-expert inference and Mimo-v2-flash, a framework for scaling efficiency. They also created T-MAC and BitNet.cpp, which utilize table lookup techniques to enable low-bit and ternary LLM inference on edge hardware. Wei completed undergraduate studies at USTC, where they researched parallel programming and program optimization in the ACSA Lab.

researcher.name: Hongshen Xu
researcher.affiliation: Xiaomi MiMo; Shanghai Jiao Tong University
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Previously Undergraduate Student @ Huazhong University of Science and Technology
researcher.bio: Hongshen Xu's MiMo scales LLM reasoning capabilities across pretraining and post-training stages. Xu is a CS PhD student at Shanghai Jiao Tong University investigating NLP, data scaling, and coding agents. They developed Chemdfm, a foundation model for chemistry, and MiMo-v2-flash, which focuses on efficient model inference. Xu also authored ACT-SQL to improve text-to-SQL tasks through automatically-generated chain-of-thought prompting. Their research includes Spider2-V, a benchmark for multimodal agents in data science workflows, and Mobile-env, an evaluation suite for LLM interactions with graphical user interfaces. Xu previously earned an undergraduate degree from Huazhong University of Science and Technology.

researcher.name: Hailin Zhang
researcher.headline: AI Infrastructure Specialist @ Xiaomi MiMo, Previously CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Hailin Zhang’s Retrieval-augmented generation for ai-generated content categorizes methods for improving generative AI through external knowledge retrieval. Currently an AI Infrastructure Specialist at Xiaomi MiMo, Zhang builds efficient RL infrastructure for the MiMo model series. They developed PQCache to manage KV caches during long-context LLM inference and created Galvatron to automate parallelism for Transformer training. Zhang also contributed to the Hetu distributed deep learning system and designed the HET framework for scaling embedding model training. They completed a PhD in CS and undergraduate degrees in CS and Economics at Peking University.

topAffiliation.description: Building efficient, scalable, and stable RL infrastructures for the MiMo series models.

researcher.name: Dong Zhang
researcher.headline: Previously Computer Science MSc Student @ Fudan University
researcher.bio: Dong Zhang’s SpeechGPT enables large language models to perceive and generate speech directly for cross-modal conversation. Zhang is a CS master's student at Fudan University supervised by Yaqian Zhou and Xipeng Qiu. Their research focuses on speech foundation models and the development of real-time human-like voice agents. Zhang also developed SpeechTokenizer, which unifies semantic and acoustic tokens for speech-centric modeling, and co-created AnyGPT to integrate text, images, speech, and music into a discrete sequence framework. They previously interned at Bytedance AI Lab researching speech translation and earned a BS in Electronic Engineering from Fudan University.

topAffiliation.description: Supervised by Prof. Yaqian Zhou and Prof. Xipeng Qiu.

researcher.name: Dawei Zhu
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Dawei Zhu co-authored Mimo-VL, a vision-language model architecture designed for multimodal reasoning and instruction following. He is a PhD student at Peking University’s School of Computer Science. His research focuses on long-context modeling, LLM agents, and alignment. In Large Language Models are not Fair Evaluators, he investigated systematic biases in using LLMs for automated scoring. Zhu also developed PaperBanana, an agentic framework that automates the generation of academic illustrations. He earned his bachelor’s degree from Peking University and has held research internships at Xiaomi, Google Cloud AI, and Microsoft Research Asia.

topAffiliation.description: Advised by Sujian Li.

researcher.name: Bowen Ye
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Bowen Ye authored MiMo to integrate reasoning capabilities into language models across both the pretraining and posttraining stages. Ye is a researcher at Peking University. Their research focus includes multimodal LLMs and autonomous agents, exemplified by the development of the Mimo-v2-flash and Mimo-audio models. To evaluate agentic systems, Ye created Claw-Eval for trustworthiness assessments and Claw-eval-live for benchmarking real-world workflows. They also work on ML systems and inference efficiency, specifically hardware-efficient attention mechanisms like HATA and expert load stabilization in MoE architectures. Additionally, Ye developed Video2GUI for synthesizing interaction trajectories to pretrain GUI agents.

researcher.name: Bowen Shen
researcher.headline: Mass Spectrometry Advisor @ Eli Lilly and Company, Previously Chemistry PhD Student @ University of Maryland
researcher.bio: Bowen Shen’s MiMo enhances the reasoning capabilities of LLMs through a unified framework for pretraining and posttraining. Shen serves as a Mass Spectrometry Advisor at Eli Lilly and Company within the Protein Characterization Team. They previously earned a PhD in Chemistry from the University of Maryland and an MSc from the University of California, Davis. In ML, Shen developed Mimo-v2-flash and Mimo-audio, which enables few-shot learning in audio language models. Their research into model efficiency produced Tailorkv for KV cache optimization and Light-PEFT for pruning parameter-efficient fine-tuning layers. Shen also investigated industrial internet of vehicles, specifically regarding edge server quantification and placement for social media service offloading.

topAffiliation.description: Protein Characterization Team, Bioproduct Research & Development

researcher.name: Boshen Xu
researcher.headline: PhD Student @ Renmin University of China, Previously CS BA Student @ University of Electronic Science and Technology of China (UESTC)
researcher.bio: Boshen Xu’s Time-r1 optimizes large vision language models for temporal video grounding through reinforcement learning post-training. He is a PhD student at Renmin University of China. His research focuses on CV and vision-and-language, specifically regarding long video understanding and egocentric perception. Xu also developed EgoDTM to integrate 3D spatial awareness into video-language pretraining and SPAFormer for sequential 3D part assembly. He previously completed a bachelor’s degree at the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China.

topAffiliation.description: Under the supervision of Professor Qin Jin at AIM3 Lab.

researcher.name: Bingquan Xia
researcher.headline: Researcher, LLM @ Xiaomi, Previously Graduate Student @ 中科院计算技术研究所
researcher.bio: Bingquan Xia's MiMo optimizes pretraining and posttraining stages to enhance reasoning capabilities in LLMs. Xia is an LLM researcher at Xiaomi, where they focus on AI infrastructure and the continued development of the MiMo model family. They worked on the Mimo-v2-flash technical report, which details an efficient, high-speed iteration of the architecture. Their research also includes Mimo-vl for multimodal processing and Mimo-audio, which enables few-shot learning in audio domains. Xia completed graduate studies at the Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, between 2018 and 2021.

topAffiliation.description: Contributed to the MiMo family of large language models.

researcher.name: Zhiyang Zhang
researcher.bio: Zhiyang Zhang co-authored EfficientRAG, an efficient retriever for multi-hop question answering. Their listed affiliation is Nanjing University, and their research areas include NLP, LLMs, agents, and AIOps. Zhang also co-authored AXIS, which uses API-first LLM agents for human-agent-computer interaction. Their work includes collaborative interfaces for personalized exploratory tasks and self-learning agents for microservice management.

researcher.name: Zhengju Tang
researcher.bio: Zhengju Tang co-authored a survey of LLMs for text-to-SQL, covering their use in translating natural-language questions into database queries. Published in ACM Computing Surveys, it is their most-cited listed work. Tang is affiliated with Peking University and works on ML systems, distributed computing, and network communication. They also contributed to TileLang, a composable tiled programming model for AI systems.

researcher.name: Yuzhe Weng
researcher.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China
researcher.headline: Researcher @ University of Science and Technology of China
researcher.bio: Yuzhe Weng developed Emotivetalk to generate expressive talking heads by decoupling audio information and applying emotional video diffusion. Weng is a researcher at the University of Science and Technology of China. Their research focuses on CV and audio-visual information fusion for digital human synthesis and multimodal sentiment analysis. They also created READ and REST, frameworks that utilize asynchronous diffusion and id-context caching to achieve real-time, streaming talking head generation. Additionally, Weng has worked on multi-label joint decoding for hierarchical fusion and methods for improving multimodal sentiment analysis through self-distillation and cross-attention.

topAffiliation.organization: University of Science and Technology of China

researcher.name: Yuheng Yang
researcher.headline: Research Engineer @ Xiaomi Mimo, Undergraduate Research Assistant @ Westlake University
researcher.bio: Yuheng Yang developed Auto-Slides, a multi-agent system that generates and customizes research presentations using academic papers. An undergraduate student at Westlake University, Yang currently serves as a Research Engineer in the Xiaomi LLM-Core Team focusing on LLM post-training and coding capabilities. Within the Westlake AGI Lab, they lead research on agents and LLMs advised by Chi Zhang. Yang also authored Probing the Knowledge Boundary, which introduces an interactive agentic framework for deep knowledge extraction from LLMs. Their background includes research internships at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and the University of California, Merced. They are pursuing a BS in Artificial Intelligence at Westlake University.

topAffiliation.description: Research on LLM post-training and coding capabilities.

researcher.name: Yuhang Wang
researcher.headline: Pretrain Data Researcher @ Xiaohongshu - Dots, Software Engineering BEng Student @ Shanghai Jiao Tong University
researcher.bio: Yuhang Wang’s SWE-Pruner adaptively prunes repository context for coding agents. They are a Pretrain Data Researcher at Xiaohongshu Dots, working on code pretraining data and midtraining for LLMs. Their AI for Software Engineering work also includes SWE-QA, which tests whether LLMs can answer repository-level code questions, and SWE-Explore, a benchmark of how coding agents explore repositories. As a ByteDance–Douyin research intern, they worked on coding agents and repository pruning; at Xiaomi MiMo, they worked on LLM training and code agents and contributed to MiMo-V2.6. They are pursuing a B.Eng. in Software Engineering at Shanghai Jiao Tong University.

topAffiliation.description: Working on pretrain data (code) and midtrain for large language models.

researcher.name: Yu Cheng
researcher.affiliation: Professor, Nanyang Technological University; Adjunct Professor, CUHK
researcher.headline: Chief Scientist @ Kunlun Wanwei Technology & Skywork AI, Lead Scientist/Professor @ Shanghai AI Lab, Lead Scientist/Professor @ Shanghai Innovation Institute
researcher.bio: Yu Cheng’s entropy mechanism uses RL to train language models for complex mathematical and physical reasoning. He is an Associate Professor at the Chinese University of Hong Kong and serves as Chief Scientist at Kunlun Wanwei and Lead Scientist at the Shanghai AI Lab. His research focuses on ML efficiency and multimodal learning, including the development of Uniter for joint image-text representation learning. Cheng also created EnlightenGAN for unsupervised low-light image enhancement and the DecodingTrust benchmark for evaluating LLM trustworthiness. Formerly a Principal Researcher at Microsoft Research Redmond and Chief Scientist at Minimax, he is scheduled to move to NTU in 2026. Cheng received his PhD from Northwestern University and his BS from Tsinghua University.

researcher.name: Yitian Gong
researcher.headline: Research Intern @ 模思智能, CS MSc Student @ Fudan University
researcher.bio: Yitian Gong’s Xy-tokenizer mitigates semantic-acoustic conflict in low-bitrate speech codecs. They are a research intern at 模思智能 and the Shanghai Innovation Institute, working on multimodal foundation models, speech tokenization, and speech generation. They are also a first author of Moss-TTS and Moss-Audio-Tokenizer, which focus on speech generation and scaling audio tokenizers for audio foundation models, respectively. Gong is a CS MSc student at Fudan University. They earned a BS in Data Science and Big Data Technology from the University of Jinan.

topAffiliation.description: Research and engineering on multimodal foundation models, speech tokenizers, speech understanding, speech generation, and large-scale distributed training.

researcher.name: Wenhao Li
researcher.bio: Wenhao Li works on AI infrastructure, including efficient LLM inference and cloud-native data systems. Their work includes binary quantization of KV caches for long-context inference. They have also studied multi-primary shared-storage databases and temporal graph storage for real-time analytics. Their Google Scholar profile lists Renmin University of China as an affiliation.

researcher.name: Taoyu Yang
researcher.headline: Undergraduate @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Taoyu Yang's Graspvla pre-trains a grasping foundation model on billion-scale synthetic action data. Yang is an undergraduate at Peking University specializing in generative AI and multimodal LLMs. Their research investigates scaling synthetic datasets for robotic manipulation and improving video synthesis through agent-based logic. This includes the development of Lighting-grounded Video Generation, a method that employs renderer-based agent reasoning. Yang has been a student at Peking University since 2022.

researcher.name: Sinan Du
researcher.headline: Master's Student @ Tsinghua University
researcher.bio: Sinan Du co-authored Intern-s1, a scientific multimodal foundation model for complex reasoning. Du is a Master’s student at Tsinghua University working on MLLMs, AIGC, and unified models. Their research investigates image tokenizers and PEFT to enhance multimodal architecture efficiency. Du also developed Chartbench, a benchmark for evaluating complex visual reasoning in chart data. They further created Chartmoe, which uses a mixture-of-experts connector to improve chart understanding.

researcher.name: Qibin Yang
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Qibin Yang's Mopd uses multi-teacher on-policy distillation to integrate capabilities during LLM post-training. They are a researcher at Peking University specializing in LLMs and Vision Language Learning. Yang also developed Claw-Eval, a framework for evaluating the trustworthiness of autonomous agents. Their research includes Griffin, which models relational databases as graph-centric foundation models. They have also investigated the application of foundation models to structured data in the context of ML and relational systems.

researcher.name: Liang Shi
researcher.affiliation: Phd Candidate of Computer Science, Peking University
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Peking University
researcher.bio: Liang Shi’s text-to-SQL survey reviews how LLMs are used to translate natural-language questions into SQL. They are a CS PhD candidate at Peking University, where they completed their undergraduate studies in 2024. Their research spans LLMs, RL, and biomolecular modeling. MiMo-V2.6 examines scaling RL toward self-improvement, while Atomic Trajectory Modeling applies state space models to biomolecular dynamics.

researcher.name: Kaiming Liu
researcher.headline: Previously CS and Technology Undergraduate Student @ Tsinghua University
researcher.bio: Kaiming Liu’s Doctor-R1 uses experiential agentic RL to conduct clinical inquiry. He is a researcher at Tsinghua University focusing on LLMs and autonomous agents. Doctor-R1 enables agents to master diagnostic questioning by learning from clinical experiences. Liu also developed Towards Unified Alignment, a framework for coordinating agent behaviors with human intent and environmental constraints. His work on AIGS introduces automated falsification to generate scientific insights, while Writing-rl applies adaptive curriculum RL to improve long-form text generation. He further researches agent-user interactions through Theory of Mind and efficient document compression for retrieval-augmented generation.

researcher.name: Kaifei Wang
researcher.bio: Kaifei Wang works on optimization, reinforcement learning, and LLMs. Their research examines training dynamics and scaling laws in associative memory learning. They also study momentum in RL with verifiable rewards and regret–instability trade-offs in multi-armed bandits. Other work addresses low-frequency alignment in VAE latent space for DiT editing.

researcher.name: Jinlong Xue
researcher.affiliation: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
researcher.headline: Previously AI MSc Student @ 北京邮电大学
researcher.bio: Jinlong Xue’s Auffusion adapts diffusion models for generating audio from text prompts. Their research spans speech synthesis, NLP, and multimodal generation, including conversational speech and context-aware text-to-speech. In RAG-TTS, they use context-aware retrieval to select speech prompts for synthesis. Xue pursued an AI master’s degree at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications through June 2025, after earning a BS there in 2022. They have also been a research intern at Microsoft and 01.AI and a visiting researcher at MBZUAI.

Liu is a research student at the University of Science and Technology of China and a researcher within the Speech Team at Alibaba’s Tongyi Lab. Based at the National Engineering Research Center of Speech and Language Information Processing, they work on TTS, Speech LLMs, and AGI. Liu developed DiffStyleTTS to perform diffusion-based hierarchical prosody modeling for controllable speech styles. They also created UDDETTS to unify discrete and dimensional emotions in emotional TTS systems. Their research includes the development of context-aware models for expressive audiobook synthesis.

researcher.bio: Hao Peng co-developed GLM-4.5, a suite of foundation models optimized for agentic reasoning and coding tasks. He is a researcher at Tsinghua University focusing on LLMs and Information Extraction. He developed LongBench v2 to evaluate reasoning and multitask performance in long-context scenarios. Peng also created KoLA to benchmark the world knowledge of language models through a curated evaluation set. In Information Extraction, he introduced MAVEN-ERE, a large-scale dataset for event coreference and causal relation extraction. His recent work on GLM-5 focuses on agentic engineering and vibe coding for foundation models.

researcher.name: Cong Wang

researcher.bio: Cong Wang created RRPO to optimize reward policies for emotional TTS using LLMs. Wang is a researcher at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications focusing on speech synthesis, speech emotion recognition, and RL applications for audio processing. They also developed HQ-SVC for high-quality zero-shot singing voice conversion and DetailTTS to capture residual information in zero-shot speech generation. In emotion recognition, Wang introduced a frame-level emotional state alignment method and investigated modal fusion strategies for multimodal data. Additional research includes the Gaitparse algorithm for self-supervised gait recognition and EEG-based Voice Conversion.

researcher.bio: Chenxu Bai created UniWorld-Design to enable layer-native design within pixel-based generative models. Bai is a Computer Science undergraduate at Peking University and a research intern at the Xiaomi MiMo team and PKU-Yuan Lab. Bai also co-developed AE2VID, a method for event-based video reconstruction using aperture modulation. Their prior experience includes research on computational photography at the Camera Intelligence Lab and scientific computing for the ABACUS project at the AI for Science Institute.

Wang is a CS PhD student at Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications and an intern at MiMo. Their research focuses on ML, LLMs, and AI Infra, specifically optimizing models for constrained environments. This includes PhyAI, which enables real-time physical AI across edge and cloud systems, and VLMCache for efficient on-device vision-language model inference. Wang also developed Quant.npu to implement fully static quantization for mobile NPUs and NanoSpec to accelerate speculative decoding.

papers.title: Mistral Large 4
papers.abstract: We introduce Mistral Large 4 (ML4), a 52B active, 1T total parameter multimodal mixture-of-experts model designed for reasoning and long-horizon agentic tasks. We build a scalable agent-based pipeline that authors and verifies executable environments for software engineering, cybersecurity, and knowledge work. Mistral Large 4 achieves competitive performance on code, cybersecurity, and held-out agentic benchmarks, including 19.7% on FrontierCode 2.0, 41% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, and 50.9% on the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index. Efficient serving combines sparse attention, optimized context parallelism, prefill–decode disaggregation, and speculative decoding. Calibrated NVFP4 quantization reduces the checkpoint to 606 GB while matching the FP8 reference on evaluations, enabling deployment on four GB300 GPUs. Multiple-teacher distillation provides high, medium, and low reasoning-effort modes, allowing users to control the trade-off between token consumption and performance.
papers.feed_description: The model’s development shows that matching language-modeling loss can mask major differences in long-horizon agent performance, making agentic evaluations essential for architecture choices.

paper_summary.summary: Mistral Large 4 is a multimodal mixture-of-experts model whose authors examine long-context attention for agentic coding. They find architecture variants with similar language-modeling loss can differ on SWE-bench Verified, while knowledge-based evaluations show no analogous gap. The final system restores long-context access in more layers and uses DSA to select past tokens; its benchmark results do not isolate DSA’s effect.

researcher.name: Abdelaziz Bounhar
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Senior AI Research Scientist / Engineer @ MBZUAI (Mohamed bin Zayed University of Artificial Intelligence)
researcher.bio: Abdelaziz Bounhar developed Nile-chat, a language model suite for Egyptian Arabic using both Arabic and Latin scripts. They are an Applied AI Scientist at Mistral AI, where they focus on RL, AI Safety, and information theory. Bounhar also created Voxtral tts for speech synthesis and Yapo, which employs sparse activation steering vectors for domain adaptation.
