In Shorter but not Worse, they introduced length regularizers to enhance the efficiency of RL for mathematical reasoning. Their research background includes investigating covert communications, as seen in Mixing a covert and a non-covert user. Bounhar earned a PhD from the Institut Polytechnique de Paris, where they researched the intersection of information theory and RL in wireless networks.

researcher.name: Aditi Kabra
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously CS PhD Student @ Carnegie Mellon University
researcher.bio: Aditi Kabra developed Verified Train Controllers to formally verify the interaction of braking and track forces within the Federal Railroad Administration kinematics model. Kabra is an AI Scientist at Mistral AI focusing on AI for formal methods and LLM-powered theorem proving. They earned a PhD in CS from Carnegie Mellon University, where they researched the automatic derivation of symbolic control constraints for cyber physical systems. This work included the creation of CESAR, a tool for control envelope synthesis using angelic refinements, and research into hybrid game control. Kabra previously designed Gator, a domain-specific language for geometry types, and studied Gaussian Boson Sampling at Cornell University. They also held engineering roles at Microsoft Azure and Google.

researcher.name: Adrien Petralia
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously PhD Researcher @ EDF R&D
researcher.bio: Adrien Petralia’s Robostral Navigate addresses robotic navigation. They are an Applied AI Scientist at Mistral AI, working on AI and time-series analysis. Their TS-ICL model uses time-indexed in-context learning for zero-shot time-series forecasting and imputation. Their work also includes NILMFormer, which accounts for non-stationarity in non-intrusive load monitoring, and methods for detecting appliances in low-frequency smart-meter data. Petralia completed a PhD in AI at Université Paris Cité while conducting research at EDF R&D.

researcher.name: Adrien Sadé
researcher.headline: Applied Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Adrien Sadé’s Ministral 3 provides a family of small language models optimized for efficient local inference. Sadé is a researcher at Mistral AI, where they focus on LLM development and multimodal architectures. They authored Stelocoder, a decoder-only model designed for multi-language to Python code translation. Sadé also worked on the Voxtral project, creating Voxtral realtime and Voxtral tts for low-latency audio processing and speech synthesis. Their work extends to vision-language models through the development of Phoenix-VL 1.5 Medium.

researcher.name: Alan Jeffares
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously ML PhD Student @ University of Cambridge
researcher.bio: Alan Jeffares co-authored Ministral 3, a Mistral preprint, and is an AI Scientist on Mistral AI’s pretraining team. Their research spans ML and statistics, including statistical learning and deep learning phenomena. In A U-turn on Double Descent, they and coauthors reconsider how parameter counting relates to model complexity and double descent. Deep Learning Through a Telescoping Lens uses a simplified model to study grokking, double descent, and gradient boosting. Jeffares completed a PhD in Applied Mathematics at the University of Cambridge, an MSc in ML at UCL, and a BSc in Statistics at University College Dublin. They previously interned with Microsoft’s deep learning team, working on discrete optimization and mixture-of-experts.

topAffiliation.description: Member of the pretraining team.

researcher.name: Albert Q. Jiang
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously CS PhD Student @ University of Cambridge
researcher.bio: Albert Q. Jiang co-developed Mistral 7B, an LLM that uses grouped-query and sliding window attention to improve inference efficiency. He is a research scientist at Mistral AI, where he works on the science and infrastructure of reasoning. His research focus includes LLMs, theorem proving, and autoformalization. Jiang also co-authored Mixtral of experts, which utilizes a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture, and Llemma, an open model for mathematical reasoning. He earned his PhD from the University of Cambridge in 2024 after studying how language models learn abstract reasoning.

topAffiliation.description: The team works on the science and infrastructure of reasoning.

researcher.name: Alexandre Gavaudan
researcher.headline: Applied Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Alexandre Gavaudan co-developed Ministral 3, a suite of LLMs designed for efficient on-device performance, as a researcher at Mistral AI. Their work focuses on developing model architectures and multimodal systems for low-latency applications. Gavaudan also worked on Voxtral realtime for speech processing and Voxtral tts for high-fidelity text-to-speech generation. This research explores the integration of language modeling and speech synthesis to build responsive AI systems. Gavaudan specializes in the optimization of compact models for high-speed inference across various hardware constraints.

researcher.name: Alexandre Laval
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Alexandre Laval works on deep learning for applied AI, including model development and benchmarking. They are an Applied AI Scientist at Mistral AI. At Thales, they conducted deep learning research in the EU CyberNemo project and contributed novel algorithms for AI and cybersecurity. Earlier, as a research assistant at Université de Technologie de Compiègne, they engineered and benchmarked facial emotion recognition models. That work aimed to quantify cognitive empathy for mixed-reality applications.

researcher.name: Alexandre Sablayrolles
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Facebook (fb.com)
researcher.bio: Alexandre Sablayrolles co-developed DeiT, a vision transformer that uses a distillation token to train efficiently on standard-sized image datasets. He is a researcher at Meta AI. His work focuses on architectural scaling for CV and LLMs, as well as methods for differential privacy and data tracing. Sablayrolles contributed to the development of Mistral 7B and Mixtral of experts, which utilize sparse mixture-of-experts to improve language model performance. He also worked on Pixtral 12B, a multimodal model that integrates vision capabilities with the Mistral architecture. His research in privacy includes the creation of Opacus, a PyTorch library for differential privacy, and Radioactive data, a technique for tracing data usage in model training.

topAffiliation.description: Contributes to the development of AI models.

researcher.name: Amélie Héliou
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Engineer @ Google
researcher.bio: Amélie Héliou works across LLMs, RL, causality, and fairness. They are an AI Scientist at Mistral AI. Before that, they were a research engineer at Google and built RL tools for training LLMs in an earlier role there. At Criteo, they held research and ML engineering roles, including work implementing NLP models for named entity recognition. Their research background includes online learning and multi-player games. They pursued a CS PhD at École Polytechnique.

researcher.name: Amos You
researcher.headline: AI Engineer / Researcher @ Mistral AI, Previously Researcher @ LinkedIn
researcher.bio: Amos You’s Ministral 3 introduces an efficient language model architecture designed for high-performance inference and compact deployment. They are an AI researcher and engineer at Mistral AI focusing on LLM post-training. You also developed TraveLER, a modular multi-LMM agent framework for video question-answering, and BlockBPE for parallelizing BPE tokenization. Their recent research includes the Voxtral series, which handles real-time audio processing and speech synthesis. Before joining Mistral AI, they worked on LLM post-training and recommender systems at LinkedIn. They earned a BS in Computer Science from UC Berkeley, where they collaborated with researchers at BAIR and Sky Computing Lab.

topAffiliation.description: Works on LLM post-training.

researcher.name: Andreas Fürst
researcher.affiliation: Johannes Kepler University Linz, Institute for Machine Learning
researcher.headline: Applied Scientist / Research Engineer @ Mistral AI, Previously PhD Researcher in Machine Learning @ Johannes Kepler University Linz
researcher.bio: Andreas Fürst's Universal Physics Transformers scales neural operators to efficiently simulate complex physical systems. Currently a PhD student at the Institute for Machine Learning at Johannes Kepler University Linz, Fürst researches ML applications in physics and contrastive learning. They also developed Cloob, an architecture that uses Modern Hopfield Networks and the InfoLOOB objective to outperform CLIP in zero-shot tasks. Their work includes Contrastive tuning, which adapts masked autoencoders, and WIND, an inverse diffusion approach for zero-shot atmospheric modeling. Additionally, Fürst created Lam-slide for modeling the latent space of spatial dynamical systems using linked entities.

researcher.name: Andrew Bai
researcher.affiliation: PhD student at Computer Science department, UCLA
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ UCLA, Previously CS BS Student @ National Taiwan University
researcher.bio: Andrew Bai’s Self-forcing++ generates high-quality video sequences at minute-scale lengths. A PhD student at UCLA, Bai researches ML, XAI, and model interpretability under advisor Cho-Jui Hsieh. Their work examines memorization and forgetting mechanisms in LLMs, specifically how supervised fine-tuning impacts context-awareness and instruction following. They also authored Concept Gradient for non-linear concept-based model interpretation and LoL for scaling video generation to hour-long durations. During internships at Google DeepMind and Nvidia, Bai developed tool-calling benchmarks and investigated catastrophic forgetting in RL-tuned reasoning models. They earned a BS in CS from National Taiwan University, where they collaborated with Kaggle on generative modeling metrics.

topAffiliation.description: Advised by Prof. Cho-Jui Hsieh; researched LLM context-awareness, catastrophic forgetting, and concept-based interpretability.

researcher.name: Andrew Zhao
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Automation PhD Student @ Tsinghua University
researcher.bio: Andrew Zhao introduced Absolute Zero to enable LLMs to learn reasoning through a self-play RL framework that requires no external training data. He is a PhD Candidate at Tsinghua University focusing on RL, language agents, and reasoning. Zhao also authored Does Reinforcement Learning Really Incentivize Reasoning Capacity to investigate whether RL-based fine-tuning improves latent reasoning or task-specific pattern matching. His work on ExpeL enables LLM agents to learn from their own experiences to improve performance across diverse tasks. In Beyond the 80/20 Rule, he identifies high-entropy minority tokens as the primary drivers of reasoning performance during RL training. His broader research includes Model Surgery for behavior modulation and ExCyTIn-Bench for evaluating agents on cyber threat investigation.

researcher.name: Andy Lo
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Andy Lo’s Pixtral 12B processes both vision and language within a 12-billion parameter multimodal architecture. Lo is a researcher at Mistral AI working on ML and large-scale generative systems. They also developed the models Magistral and Voxtral, which have emerged as breakout works in generative modeling. Their research on End-to-end ontology learning with large language models uses LLMs to automate the creation of structured knowledge bases. Lo further investigates training efficiency, specifically the methods introduced in Efficient Sparse Training with Structured Dropout.

topAffiliation.description: Co-leading the runtime team

researcher.name: Anmol Agarwal
researcher.headline: Previously NLP/ML MSc Student @ Carnegie Mellon University
researcher.bio: Anmol Agarwal co-created Magistral, a large language model developed while serving as an AI scientist intern at Mistral AI. Agarwal is an MSc student in NLP and ML at Carnegie Mellon University. Their research focus includes LLMs and code generation, featuring works like Voxtral for real-time audio and Devstral for fine-tuning coding agents. Previously, Agarwal was a research fellow in the AI4Code group at Microsoft Research India, where they worked on Verus-SpecGym for specification autoformalization. They also developed ChaTA, an intelligent question-answer teaching assistant using open-source models. Agarwal holds a BTech from IIIT-Hyderabad and conducted earlier research on information retrieval and clinical NLP within the Precog Lab.

researcher.name: Antonia Calvi
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Mistral AI, Previously Researcher @ atla
researcher.bio: Antonia Calvi co-developed Ministral 3, a compact LLM optimized for edge-based inference. Calvi is currently a Researcher at Mistral AI, where they focus on efficient language modeling and audio systems. Their recent contributions include the Voxtral series for real-time audio and text-to-speech, alongside the safety-oriented Shieldstral. Before Mistral, Calvi was a Researcher at atla, where they worked on Atla Selene Mini, a general-purpose model-as-a-judge for automated evaluation. During their tenure as an AI Research Scientist at Exscientia, they co-authored Leap, a method for scoring molecular synthesisability in drug discovery. Calvi also served as a Task Manager at Omdena between 2019 and 2024.

researcher.name: Arjun Majumdar
researcher.headline: Previously Research Scientist @ Meta AI (FAIR Robotics)
researcher.bio: Arjun Majumdar’s Beyond the nav-graph enables agents to navigate continuous 3D environments using visual observations and natural language instructions. A Research Scientist at Meta AI in the FAIR Robotics team, they specialize in scaling robot learning through world models and Embodied AI. Majumdar co-developed OpenEQA, an open-vocabulary benchmark for embodied question answering, and ZSON, which provides zero-shot object-goal navigation via multimodal embeddings. They earned a PhD from Georgia Tech under Dhruv Batra and completed research internships at Google Robotics, Amazon Alexa AI, and FAIR. Their work also includes Locate 3D, a self-supervised framework for localizing objects in real-world 3D environments from language descriptions. Majumdar previously held research and engineering roles at MIT Lincoln Laboratory and Northrop Grumman after studying at the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign.

topAffiliation.description: Explored scaling robot learning through developing robotic world models; developed methods for locating objects in 3D indoor environments from referring expressions.

researcher.name: Arthur Fournier
researcher.headline: Applied AI Engineer @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Arthur Fournier's Voxtral TTS synthesizes speech from text as a generative audio model. Fournier is a researcher at Mistral AI. Their research focuses on speech synthesis and the development of generative audio systems. Voxtral TTS represents their primary contribution to text-to-speech technology. They are based at Mistral AI, where they work on audio and speech modeling.

researcher.name: Artjom Joosen
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Researcher @ Huawei Research UK
researcher.bio: Artjom Joosen’s Voxtral tts performs text-to-speech synthesis using a foundation model architecture. At Mistral AI, Joosen researches LLMs, time series forecasting, and cloud computing. They co-authored How does it function?, an analysis of long-term trends in production serverless workloads. Joosen also developed Dam, a foundation model for time series forecasting. Their other work explores serverless cold starts, Lightweight online adaption, and speculative decoding with randomized drafting.

researcher.name: Avinash Sooriyarachchi
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Senior Solutions Architect @ Databricks
researcher.bio: Avinash Sooriyarachchi’s Ministral 3 consists of efficient small language models designed for edge computing and on-device ML tasks. Currently a researcher at Mistral AI, they focus on the development of LLMs and multimodal architectures. Sooriyarachchi contributed to Voxtral, a suite for real-time speech processing and text-to-speech generation. Their research portfolio also includes Shieldstral, a model for content safety, and Robostral Navigate for robotic navigation. Additionally, they have authored technical guides on optimizing LLM performance using LoRA fine-tuning.

topAffiliation.description: Collaborates with engineering and research teams to develop effective AI systems for enterprise companies and startups.

researcher.name: Baptiste Roziere
researcher.headline: CodeGen Lead @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Meta AI
researcher.bio: Baptiste Roziere co-authored Llama, a suite of open foundation models trained on large-scale datasets for general-purpose language tasks. Now a researcher at Mistral AI, his work centers on LLMs, code generation, and language modeling. He contributed to the development of Llama 3, which scales dense Transformer architectures to hundreds of billions of parameters for improved reasoning and dialogue. Roziere led research on Code Llama, a version of these models specialized for programming and long-context tasks. He also introduced Multi-token prediction to improve the efficiency of LLM training and inference by predicting multiple tokens simultaneously. His recent projects include the multimodal model Pixtral 12B and CruxEval, a benchmark for assessing code reasoning and execution.

researcher.name: Chris Bamford
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Senior Research Engineer @ modl.ai
researcher.bio: Chris Bamford co-authored Mixtral of experts, which employs a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture to scale parameter counts while maintaining low inference costs. They are a researcher at Mistral AI, where they focus on RL, robotics, and the development of LLMs. Bamford also contributed to Mistral 7B, an architecture utilizing grouped-query and sliding window attention. Their earlier research in Game AI produced Griddly, a flexible platform for grid-world RL, and Gym-µrts for real-time strategy benchmarks. Recent work includes Magistral and Devstral, a model fine-tuned for coding agent applications.

researcher.name: Clémence Lanfranchi
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Member of Technical Staff @ Oracle Labs
researcher.bio: Clémence Lanfranchi co-developed Magistral, a large language model that balances reasoning performance with efficient inference. Currently a researcher at Mistral AI, they focus on the architecture and fine-tuning of LLMs for specialized tasks and diverse modalities. Lanfranchi contributed to Ministral 3, a family of small-footprint models, and Voxtral, which enables real-time speech processing and audio generation. Their work includes Devstral, a model fine-tuned for coding agent applications, and Distill-C, a framework for improving NL2SQL performance via distilled customization. They previously researched attention mechanisms for fraud detection in graph dynamics and developed synthetic tabular metadata generators using LLMs. Lanfranchi also holds patents for execution-based feedback in automated test generation and LLM-based SQL data augmentation.

researcher.name: Connor Chen
researcher.bio: Connor Chen is an ML researcher whose work includes evaluating reward models for RLHF and adapting LLM evaluations to prompts. Their listed affiliation is UC Berkeley. They have also worked on disentangling sentiment from substance in LLM outputs. In related work, they studied how people combine heuristics and Bayesian inference when exploring under uncertainty.

researcher.name: Corentin Barreau
researcher.headline: Applied AI Engineer @ Mistral AI, Previously Software Engineer @ Internet Archive
researcher.bio: Corentin Barreau co-developed Ministral 3, a family of small LLMs designed for efficient on-device inference. They are a researcher at Mistral AI where they work on ML and web archiving. Barreau’s research also includes the development of Voxtral, a suite of models for real-time audio processing and text-to-speech tasks. Additionally, they contributed to Devstral, which applies fine-tuning techniques to adapt language models for coding agent use cases. Their work focuses on scaling efficiency and specialized model performance across diverse modalities.

researcher.name: Corentin Sautier
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously CV PhD Student @ ENPC
researcher.bio: Corentin Sautier developed Image-to-lidar self-supervised distillation, which transfers representations from images to LiDAR point clouds to train autonomous driving models without manual labels. Sautier is a researcher at ENPC and valeo.ai working on CV and 3D representation learning. His work focuses on improving LiDAR feature extraction through cross-modal distillation and geometric priors. He authored ALSO, which uses occupancy estimation for LiDAR self-supervision, and Bevcontrast, a method for contrastive learning in bird’s-eye view space. Sautier also created Three pillars to refine the distillation of vision foundation models into point clouds. His recent research includes Clustering is back, which evaluates training-free LiDAR instance segmentation, and UNIT, a framework for unsupervised online instance segmentation.

researcher.name: Dhia Garbaya
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Visiting Student @ EPFL
researcher.bio: Dhia Garbaya contributed to Falcon 3, a family of open-source LLMs developed using pruning and distillation during their time on the AI theory team at TII. During a long visit at EPFL's MLO lab, they joined the Swiss AI Initiative core LLM team. Dhia co-authored Apertus (Swiss LLM) to promote open LLMs across global language environments and developed FOG for training LLMs using fully FP8 matmuls. Their work also includes Terminator, which identifies optimal exit points to reduce overthinking in CoT reasoning. Currently a research scientist intern at Mistral AI, Dhia focuses on long-horizon RL and reports to Albert Jiang. They contributed to Leanstral-1.5 and Mistral Large 4 models.

topAffiliation.description: Research scientist intern working on long-horizon reinforcement learning, reporting to Albert Jiang.

researcher.name: Emmanuel Gottlob
researcher.headline: Machine Learning Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Physics PhD Student @ University of Cambridge
researcher.bio: Emmanuel Gottlob's One-to-one quantum simulation uses a 256-qubit programmable simulator to model the properties of the frustrated magnet TmMgGaO. Now at Mistral AI, Gottlob is a researcher in ML who previously developed the circulant matrix model at EPFL to describe beam instabilities in synchrotrons. Gottlob also authored Hubbard models, which identifies effective Hamiltonians for particles in optical quasicrystals. Their research includes Simulating dynamics of the two-dimensional transverse-field Ising model, a comparative study of classical numerical techniques for quantum dynamics. Gottlob’s work integrates many-body physics with computational simulation and ML.

researcher.name: Faruk Ahmed
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Google
researcher.bio: Faruk Ahmed co-authored Improved training of Wasserstein GANs, which introduces a gradient penalty to stabilize the training of generative adversarial networks. Currently an AI Scientist at Mistral, he focuses on ML and the development of multimodal LLMs. Ahmed contributed to Gemini 2.5, a model designed for advanced reasoning, long-context processing, and next-generation agentic capabilities. He also worked on the development of Ministral 3 and PathAlign, a vision-language model for whole slide images in histopathology. Ahmed’s earlier research includes PixelVAE for image generation and methods for reducing overfitting by decorrelating deep network representations. He has additionally explored systematic generalization through group invariant predictions and semantic anomaly detection.

researcher.name: Federico Baldassarre
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Postdoctoral Researcher @ Meta
researcher.bio: Federico Baldassarre’s DINOv3 scales self-supervised vision models to 7 billion parameters to achieve high-quality dense representations. He is an AI Scientist at Mistral AI where he focuses on multimodal LLMs and video foundation models. During his tenure at Meta FAIR, Baldassarre authored Back to the Features to train latent video world models within the feature space of DINOv2. He also contributed to DINOv2 Meets Text, a framework that aligns vision and language at both the image and pixel levels. His earlier research includes Explainability Techniques for Graph Convolutional Networks, developed during his PhD at KTH Royal Institute of Technology. At Mistral, his work has expanded into generative audio and speech through the Voxtral models.

topAffiliation.description: Works on multimodal foundation models for vision and language.

researcher.name: Gaspard Beaudouin
researcher.affiliation: Mistral AI - École nationale des ponts et chaussées, Institut Polytechnique de Paris
researcher.headline: Research Scientist Intern @ Mistral AI, Mathematics, CV and ML MSc Student @ ENS Paris-Saclay
researcher.bio: Gaspard Beaudouin’s Page-4d performs 4D perception by disentangling pose and geometry estimation. They are a Research Scientist Intern on the Multimodal team at Mistral AI and a Master’s student in the MVA program at ENS Paris-Saclay. Beaudouin's research centers on generative modeling and flow matching, including the development of Delta Rectified Flow Sampling for text-to-image editing. They also co-authored SplitFlow, which utilizes flow decomposition for inversion-free image manipulation. Previously, Beaudouin researched agentic LLMs at Sinequa and investigated flow matching at the Harvard AI and Robotics Lab. They completed their undergraduate studies in mathematics and computer science at École nationale des ponts et chaussées.

topAffiliation.description: Worked on the Multimodal team, focusing on Vision Encoder.

researcher.name: Gauthier Guinet
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral Ai, Previously Applied Scientist @ AWS AI Labs, Amazon
researcher.bio: Gauthier Guinet co-developed Magistral, a large language model released by Mistral AI. They are a Research Scientist at Mistral AI, where they focus on RL and the development of code agents. Guinet also contributed to Ministral 3 and Voxtral, a model family designed for speech processing and real-time audio generation. Their research includes Devstral, which fine-tunes LLMs for coding applications, and Task-Specific Exam Generation for the automated evaluation of retrieval-augmented models. Additionally, Guinet authored Execution-Free Evaluation of Code Changes to assess code edits using LLM critics. Earlier work at MIT addressed bandit problems under censorship and Pareto-efficient acquisition for Bayesian optimization.

researcher.name: Giada Pistilli
researcher.headline: Multilingual Team Lead @ Mistral, Previously Principal Ethicist @ Hugging Face
researcher.bio: Giada Pistilli co-led the ethical and legal development of Bloom, an open-access multilingual model trained on 46 natural languages. They currently lead the Multilingual team within Science at Mistral AI. Previously, Pistilli served as Principal Ethicist at Hugging Face, where they managed interdisciplinary research on AI ethics and open-source development. Their research focuses on how cultural values and social norms are encoded in LLMs, as explored through the ROOTS Corpus and the CIVICS dataset for culturally-informed value alignment. They also developed INTIMA, a benchmark for evaluating human-AI companionship and relational behaviors. Pistilli earned a PhD in Philosophy from Sorbonne Université-CNRS, where they studied the ethics of conversational AI.

topAffiliation.description: Leads the multilingual pipeline across pretraining and post-training.

researcher.name: Guillaume Kunsch
researcher.headline: Applied Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously AI Research Engineer, LLM @ Technology Innovation Institute
researcher.bio: Guillaume Kunsch developed Ministral 3, a family of small-scale language models designed for edge and on-device deployment. They are a researcher at Mistral AI focusing on deep learning and the development of efficient LLM architectures. Kunsch contributed to Falcon Mamba, an attention-free 7B model that uses a linear-time sequence mechanism to process long contexts. They also worked on Falcon-H1, which uses a hybrid-head design to balance computational speed and model performance. Their recent work in audio includes the Voxtral series, specifically Voxtral Realtime and Voxtral TTS for low-latency speech synthesis. Kunsch also co-authored the Phoenix-VL 1.5 technical report on multimodal vision-language models.

researcher.name: Guillaume Lample
researcher.headline: Co-Founder and Chief Science Officer @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Facebook AI Research
researcher.bio: Guillaume Lample co-developed Llama, a collection of open foundation LLMs designed for efficient performance on consumer hardware. Currently a researcher at Mistral AI, he led the development of Mistral 7B and Mixtral of experts, a model utilizing a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture. His research focuses on scaling LLMs, unsupervised machine translation, and the application of neural networks to symbolic mathematics. Lample’s earlier contributions include Neural architectures for named entity recognition and the development of the NuminaMath dataset for mathematical reasoning. He has also worked extensively on cross-lingual representations and the unsupervised translation of programming languages.

researcher.name: Gunjan Dhanuka
researcher.headline: AI Research Scientist @ Mistral, Previously Graduate Student Researcher, ML @ CMU
researcher.bio: Gunjan Dhanuka's Voxtral tts generates synthetic speech through large-scale audio modeling. Dhanuka is a Research Scientist at Mistral AI specializing in multimodal models and trustworthy ML. They also developed Voxtral realtime for low-latency audio processing and MAGIC, which audits memorization in diffusion models via generative image compression. Other research includes Distilling Aggregated Knowledge for anomaly detection in weakly-supervised video datasets. Dhanuka earned an MSCS from Carnegie Mellon University and a B.Tech. from the Indian Institute of Technology, Guwahati.

researcher.name: Gunshi Gupta
researcher.affiliation: Research scientist @ Mistral AI, Ph.D at University of Oxford
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously ML DPhil Student @ University of Oxford
researcher.bio: Gunshi Gupta's Ministral 3 introduces a family of small-scale LLMs designed for high-performance edge computing. They are a research scientist at Mistral AI and a PhD candidate at the University of Oxford. Gupta's work centers on RL and multi-modal learning, specifically designing memory-augmented architectures to enable agents to perform long-horizon tasks. They also developed La-MAML, an algorithm that applies meta-learning to online continual learning to manage non-stationary data streams. Additional research includes Memo, a framework for training memory-efficient embodied agents, and the Findingdory evaluation benchmark. Previously, they conducted ML research at Wayve and Microsoft Research and earned a master's degree from Mila.

researcher.name: Han Zhou
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Student Researcher @ Google DeepMind
researcher.bio: I am a Research Scientist at Mistral AI, where I work on coding agents and LLM post-training. Previously, I was a Student Researcher at Google DeepMind, working on self-improving agents. I hold an MEng in Engineering Science from the University of Oxford and am a PhD candidate in NLP at the University of Cambridge.

researcher.name: Hugo Thimonier
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously ML Research Scientist @ Emobot
researcher.bio: Hugo Thimonier’s T-JEPA enables self-supervised learning on tabular data through a joint embedding predictive architecture that avoids manual data augmentations. Thimonier is an Applied AI Scientist at Mistral focusing on multimodal LLMs. Their research in structured data includes Beyond Individual Input, which identifies anomalies by analyzing relationships across multiple data points rather than individual samples. They also developed EmoSLLM for parameter-efficient speech emotion recognition and Voxtral tts for multimodal speech generation. Thimonier holds a PhD in Computer Science from CentraleSupélec and the LISN Lab and previously studied at ENS Paris-Saclay and ENSAE.

topAffiliation.description: Works on multimodal and agentic LLMs.

researcher.name: Jacques Sun
researcher.headline: Applied Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Jacques Sun’s Voxtral tts generates synthetic audio by mapping text to speech in a generative framework. Sun is a researcher at Mistral AI focusing on AI and speech technology. Their work on Voxtral tts explores the integration of linguistic modeling with acoustic synthesis. Sun operates within Mistral AI’s research division, where they develop ML systems for audio generation. This work represents their primary contribution to generative modeling and speech synthesis.

topAffiliation.description: Worked on a master’s thesis.

researcher.name: Jan Ludziejewski
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously ML PhD Student @ University of Warsaw
researcher.bio: Jan Ludziejewski’s Scaling Laws for Fine-Grained MoE characterizes performance trends relative to expert granularity in sparse neural networks. Ludziejewski is a researcher at Mistral AI where they focus on MoE architectures, LLMs, and scaling laws. They co-developed Moe-mamba, which integrates MoE with selective state space models to optimize sequence modeling. Their research also includes the development of the Magistral and Ministral 3 models, alongside the Voxtral audio model series. Ludziejewski has further investigated memory efficiency in Joint moe scaling laws and continuous routing mechanisms in Mixture of tokens.

topAffiliation.description: Pretraining

researcher.name: Jason Rute
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Postdoctoral Researcher, Mathematics of AI @ IBM Research
researcher.bio: Jason Rute’s A formal proof of the Kepler conjecture provides a computer-verified certification of the sphere-packing density bound. They are an AI researcher at Mistral AI and formerly worked as a mathematician and data scientist at IBM Research. Rute’s work focuses on AI reasoning and automated theorem proving, including the development of LLMs such as Magistral, Ministral 3, and Voxtral. They also developed Proof artifact co-training to train models on the intermediate steps of formal proofs and Graph2Tac for representing mathematical concepts. Rute holds a PhD from Carnegie Mellon University and has published research on computability theory, proof theory, and algorithmic randomness.

researcher.name: Jessica Chudnovsky
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously CS MSc Student @ Stanford University
researcher.bio: Jessica Chudnovsky’s Pixtral 12B is a multimodal model that integrates vision and text processing within a 12-billion parameter architecture. They are a Research Scientist at Mistral AI and a CS MSc student at Stanford University. Chudnovsky also developed Voxtral and researches the mechanics of LLM truthfulness. In Consensus is not verification, they demonstrate why crowd-wisdom strategies fail to serve as reliable proxies for factual accuracy. Their work on data scaling, including Internal Data Repetition Destroys Language Models, examines how repeated sequences in training sets degrade model performance. Chudnovsky holds undergraduate degrees from Stanford in Math and Computational Science and Symbolic Systems.

topAffiliation.description: Contributed to the Pixtral 12B multimodal language model.

researcher.name: John Harvill
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Applied Scientist @ Amazon Web Services (AWS)
researcher.bio: John Harvill's Meta-Tokens introduces lossless token sequence compression to improve the efficiency of LLMs. Currently an AI Scientist at Mistral AI, they focus on advancing speech and audio understanding for generative models. Harvill earned a PhD in EE from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign in 2024. Their research includes Synthesis of new words, which expands training vocabularies to improve dysarthric speech recognition. They also developed LI-TTA for language-informed test-time adaptation in automatic speech recognition. Harvill's broader work focuses on acoustic analysis for health monitoring and frame-level stutter detection.

topAffiliation.description: Advancing speech and audio understanding in LLMs.

researcher.name: Julien Denize
researcher.headline: Research Engineer @ Mistral AI, Previously Machine Learning Engineer @ CEA List
researcher.bio: Julien Denize’s Magistral provides multimodal generation and reasoning capabilities within open-source model frameworks. They are a Research Engineer at Mistral AI, where they build LLMs for coding and maintain open-source libraries including vLLM and Transformers. Denize also authored Devstral, which fine-tunes models for coding agents, and Voxtral. Their research focuses on self-supervised learning and CV, notably the development of Similarity contrastive estimation for soft contrastive learning. Denize holds a PhD from Normandie Université, where they studied self-supervised representation learning for image and video analysis. They previously worked at CEA List as an ML Engineer, managing MLOps workflows and leading the Pixano data annotation project.

topAffiliation.description: Worked on open-source models for multimodal generation, reasoning, and coding agents; developed internal tooling, maintained open-source libraries, and contributed to vLLM and Transformers.

researcher.name: Khyathi Raghavi Chandu
researcher.headline: AI Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Allen Institute for AI
researcher.bio: Khyathi Raghavi Chandu co-created Rewardbench to evaluate the reward models used for LLM alignment. She is an AI Research Scientist at Mistral AI, where she leads the development of the Magistral reasoning models and the Voxtral audio-language model family. Her research focuses on NLP, multimodality, and training large-scale models ranging from 3B to 123B parameters. Previously, she contributed to the open-source OLMo and Dolma projects at the Allen Institute for AI and held a research role at Meta AI. Chandu earned her PhD from the Language Technologies Institute at Carnegie Mellon University, specializing in grounded multimodal long-form generation. She also developed Wildbench to benchmark LLMs using challenging tasks from real-world users.

topAffiliation.description: Developing and training large-scale models, including the Voxtral audio-language models and Magistral reasoning models, and advancing open-source research and releases.

researcher.name: Kush Jain
researcher.headline: AI Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Software Engineering PhD Student @ Carnegie Mellon University
researcher.bio: Kush Jain's CAT-LM trains LLMs on aligned code and test sequences. An AI research scientist at Mistral AI, Jain focuses on ML for software engineering and program analysis, having co-developed the Magistral and Ministral 3 models. They also created Testgeneval, a benchmark for real-world unit test generation and completion. Jain holds a PhD in software engineering from Carnegie Mellon University, where they were advised by Claire Le Goues. Their prior research at UT Austin applied mutation testing to formal verification by mutating proof definitions to identify incomplete specifications.

topAffiliation.description: Works on code agents, including synthetic data generation, human data annotation, and the curation of RL environments at scale.

researcher.name: Laurence Aitchison
researcher.headline: Head of Reasoning @ Mistral AI, Previously Senior Lecturer, AI @ University of Bristol
researcher.bio: Laurence Aitchison’s Bayesian low-rank adaptation integrates probabilistic inference into LLM fine-tuning to improve uncertainty quantification. He is the Head of Reasoning at Mistral AI and a Senior Lecturer at the University of Bristol researching the intersection of Bayesian ML and deep learning. His work on Deep convolutional networks as shallow Gaussian processes establishes a theoretical correspondence between finite architectures and kernel methods. Aitchison contributed to the development of Ministral 3, an LLM optimized for reasoning and local deployment. He also authored A statistical theory of cold posteriors to explain performance gains from posterior tempering in Bayesian deep learning. He completed his PhD at the Gatsby Computational Neuroscience Unit at UCL and previously served as a postdoctoral researcher at the University of Cambridge.

researcher.name: Laurent Fainsin
researcher.headline: Applied Science Engineer @ Mistral AI, Previously Machine Learning Engineer @ Finegrain
researcher.bio: Laurent Fainsin co-developed Ministral 3, a series of small language models designed for efficient local deployment and low-latency inference. They are an ML researcher at Mistral AI and a student at ENSEEIHT. Fainsin’s work focuses on generative modeling, including the development of Voxtral realtime and Voxtral tts for live audio processing and speech synthesis. Their earlier research involved Neural detection of spheres, a CV method for automating lighting calibration in industrial settings. This project applied deep learning to geometric detection to streamline quality control processes. Fainsin’s research interests center on the optimization and architectural design of generative systems.

researcher.name: Lingxiao Zhao
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Zoom
researcher.bio: Lingxiao Zhao co-developed Chain of draft, which uses minimalist intermediate reasoning to accelerate LLM inference. He is an AI Scientist at Mistral AI focusing on generative models and LLM pretraining. His earlier research includes Beyond homophily, which investigates GNN performance on graphs where neighboring nodes have different labels. Zhao also created Pairnorm to mitigate oversmoothing in deep graph networks and Pard for permutation-invariant graph generation. He earned a PhD in Machine Learning from Carnegie Mellon University and previously worked as a research scientist at Zoom. His background includes research internships at Apple, NVIDIA, and Snap Inc.

researcher.name: Louis Martin
researcher.headline: Staff Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Technical Lead, AI Safety @ Meta
researcher.bio: Louis Martin co-authored CamemBERT, a French language model. They are a Staff Research Scientist at Mistral AI, where they previously led post-training. Their work spans LLMs, NLP, and text simplification, including ASSET, a dataset for evaluating sentence simplification, and MUSS, a method for multilingual unsupervised simplification. During their PhD at Inria and Facebook AI, they studied controllable and unsupervised approaches to sentence simplification and tools for people with cognitive disabilities. At Meta, they also worked on LLM safety.

researcher.name: Luyu Gao
researcher.headline: Researcher @ OpenAI, NLP PhD Student @ Carnegie Mellon University
researcher.bio: Luyu Gao’s Self-refine enables LLMs to improve their own outputs by iteratively generating feedback and refining responses. Gao is a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon University in the Language Technologies Institute, working with Jamie Callan. His research spans IR, representation learning, and LLM reasoning. He co-developed PAL, which offloads reasoning steps to a program interpreter to improve problem-solving. He also created SciCode, a research coding benchmark curated by scientists, and Active retrieval augmented generation. Gao graduated from the University of Illinois at Urbana Champaign in Computer Science and previously interned with the Nvidia GPU foundation profiler team.

researcher.name: Maarten Buyl
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Postdoctoral Researcher, AI @ Ghent University
researcher.bio: Maarten Buyl co-developed Ministral 3, a family of small language models designed for local inference and edge computing applications. Buyl is an AI Scientist at Mistral AI where they research LLMs, AI safety, and algorithmic fairness. They authored Debayes, which uses a Bayesian approach to mitigate bias in network embeddings by separating sensitive attributes from latent representations. Their work also includes Large language models reflect the ideology of their creators, an empirical study of how developer preferences influence model biases, and the Voxtral series for speech synthesis and real-time audio. Additionally, Buyl has analyzed AI alignment through Ai alignment at your discretion and developed fairret, a framework for differentiable fairness regularization in ML.

researcher.name: Matthieu Dinot
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously CS MSc Student @ École Polytechnique - MVA
researcher.bio: Matthieu Dinot co-authored Ministral 3, a family of small-scale language models optimized for edge-device deployment. Currently an AI Scientist at Mistral AI, Dinot works on the code generation and reasoning team using RL. Their research focuses on scaling model capabilities, including the large-scale model Magistral and the coding-agent framework Devstral. Dinot also contributed to the voice-based model Voxtral, which handles speech-to-speech and text-to-speech tasks. They previously held a research internship at INRIA and earned a CS MSc from the MVA program at École Polytechnique.

topAffiliation.description: Worked in the code generation and reasoning team (RL).

researcher.name: Matthieu Futeral
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously NLP PhD Student @ Inria
researcher.bio: Matthieu Futeral co-created Ministral 3, a family of language models optimized for edge devices and low-latency performance. They are an AI Scientist at Mistral AI specializing in ML, NLP, CV, and speech. In multimodal machine translation, Futeral authored Tackling ambiguity with images to resolve linguistic uncertainty using visual context. They also developed speech systems including Voxtral tts and Voxtral realtime. Other research includes mOSCAR, a multilingual and multimodal document-level corpus, and the construction of treebanks for North-African Arabizi.

researcher.name: Maxime Darrin
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Information Theory and ML PhD Student @ MILA - INSTITUT QUÉBÉCOIS D'INTELLIGENCE ARTIFICIELLE, Information Theory and ML PhD Student @ UNIVERSITÉ PARIS-SACLAY
researcher.bio: Maxime Darrin co-developed Magistral, a large language model that performs LLM reasoning. Darrin is a PhD candidate at MILA, McGill University, and Paris-Saclay University, and is affiliated with Mistral AI. Their research focus includes reasoning LLMs, RL, and the robustness of text generation. Other notable works include the Ministral 3 model and Voxtral, a family of models for real-time speech and text processing. To improve model reliability, Darrin created RainProof to shield generators from out-of-distribution data and developed unsupervised layer-wise aggregation for OOD detection. They hold master’s degrees from Sorbonne Université and ENS de Lyon, alongside an engineering degree from Mines Paris.

researcher.name: Maximilian Augustin
researcher.headline: Previously PhD Student @ University of Tuebingen
researcher.bio: Maximilian Augustin’s Diffusion Visual Counterfactual Explanations uses generative diffusion to explain model predictions through image-space counterfactuals. He is a PhD student at the University of Tuebingen. His research focuses on CV, LLMs, and the interpretability of deep learning systems. Augustin developed the Magistral and Ministral 3 language models, as well as the Voxtral series for speech and audio processing. His work also includes Dash, a framework for detecting systematic hallucinations in VLMs, and Mlcapsule, a system for secure offline ML deployment. He has further contributed to research on adversarial robustness and methods for out-of-distribution detection.

researcher.name: Mert Unsal
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Founding Engineer @ Browser Use
researcher.bio: Mert Unsal’s Kimina-Prover applies long chain-of-thought RL to formal theorem proving. Now an AI Scientist at Mistral and an MSc student at ETH Zurich, Unsal previously developed the agentic model BU-30B-A3B-Preview while a researcher at Browser Use. Their work at SRI Lab focused on AlphaIntegrator, a neurosymbolic system for step-by-step symbolic integration. During a tenure at Huawei Paris, Unsal built FlexTrain, a dynamic training framework for heterogeneous environments presented at NeurIPS 2023. They hold a BSc in Mathematics and Economics from École Polytechnique and previously worked on option pricing as a quantitative trader at SIG.

researcher.name: Mia Chiquier
researcher.headline: CS PhD Student @ Columbia University
researcher.bio: Mia Chiquier's Ministral 3 introduces a family of language models optimized for efficient reasoning and inference. She is a PhD student at Columbia University advised by Carl Vondrick, where she researches ML methods for controlling multimodal generative models. Her work includes Real-time neural voice camouflage, which generates acoustic perturbations to prevent microphones from successfully recording speech for automatic recognition. In CV, her research on Adversarial attacks are reversible with natural supervision uses self-supervised signals to restore images corrupted by adversarial perturbations. She also developed Evolving interpretable visual classifiers with LLMs to automate the creation of transparent recognition programs. Chiquier previously graduated from the University of Pennsylvania and focuses on applications in machine teaching.

topAffiliation.description: Advised by Carl Vondrick; works on machine learning methods for controlling multimodal generative models, particularly for machine teaching.

researcher.name: Minh-Quang PHAM
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Zoom Communications
researcher.bio: Minh-Quang PHAM developed Voxtral tts to generate speech through specialized language models. They are an Applied AI Scientist at Mistral AI, where they work on post-training RL for cybersecurity coding agents. Previously, Pham was a Research Scientist at Zoom focused on spoken language technology and Voxtral realtime. Their research in NLP includes Revisiting multi-domain machine translation, which evaluates model performance across diverse data distributions. They also co-authored Select, prompt, filter to distill LLMs for conversation summarization. Pham earned a PhD in NLP from Université Paris-Saclay and is a graduate of École Polytechnique and Télécom ParisTech.

topAffiliation.description: Works on post-training coding agents for cybersecurity using reinforcement learning, including cybench and cybergym.

researcher.name: Minwoo Kang
researcher.headline: Previously CS PhD Student @ University of California, Berkeley
researcher.bio: Research @ Mistral; PhD @ UC Berkeley

topAffiliation.description: Conducted research with John Canny and John Wawrzynek through Berkeley AI Research (BAIR).

researcher.name: Morgane Riviere
researcher.headline: Staff Research Engineer @ Google DeepMind, Previously Research Engineer @ Facebook
researcher.bio: Morgane Riviere helped develop Gemini, a family of multimodal models that integrates processing for text, images, and audio. Currently a researcher at Google DeepMind, she focuses on deep learning, CV, and ASR. She co-authored Gemma 3, a suite of open models designed for multimodal reasoning and agentic capabilities. Her previous research includes the creation of VoxPopuli, a large-scale multilingual speech corpus, and Libri-light, a benchmark for ASR under limited supervision. Riviere also co-created Open Catalyst 2020, a dataset for applying ML to renewable energy storage and electrocatalyst design. Her work emphasizes building the large-scale datasets and benchmarks necessary to advance representation learning across modalities.

researcher.name: Nathan Grinsztajn
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ MISTRAL AI, Previously Member of Technical Staff @ COHERE
researcher.bio: Nathan Grinsztajn co-developed Command a, an enterprise-ready LLM designed for business applications. Now a Research Scientist at Mistral AI, they focus on agents following a role as a Member of Technical Staff at Cohere. Grinsztajn’s research includes Should we be going MAD?, which evaluates multi-agent debate strategies for LLM reasoning, and Jumanji, a suite of hardware-accelerated RL environments. They also authored Winner Takes It All, a method for training RL populations for combinatorial optimization. Grinsztajn earned a PhD in RL from Inria, where they researched discrete problems and graph representation.

topAffiliation.description: Work on agents.

researcher.name: Neeraj Ong Aggarwal
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, prev Applied Intuition

researcher.name: Neha Gupta
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Neha Gupta’s Magistral provides a large-scale language model architecture for Mistral AI. Currently an AI Scientist at Mistral AI, Gupta researches LLM efficiency, model cascades, and audio synthesis. They contributed to the development of Ministral 3 and the Voxtral series, which includes the Voxtral TTS text-to-speech system. Their work on Language Model Cascades examines token-level uncertainty, while Faster Cascades via Speculative Decoding optimizes inference speeds. Gupta’s earlier research investigated implicit regularization in deep neural networks and optimization for decision tree induction.

topAffiliation.description: Focuses on pretraining and advancing the capabilities of large language models.

researcher.name: Nikhil Raghuraman
researcher.headline: Member of Technical Staff @ OpenAI, Previously AI Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Nikhil Raghuraman co-authored Pixtral 12B, a multimodal model designed to process interleaved image and text inputs. They are an AI Scientist at Mistral AI, where they contribute to the development of specialized LLMs such as Magistral and Ministral 3. Their research also extends to the speech-centric Voxtral and Devstral, a model fine-tuned for coding agent applications. Beyond language modeling, Raghuraman researches CV, notably developing Alltracker for high-resolution dense point tracking. Previously a software engineer at Jane Street, they earned a Bachelor’s and Master’s in Computer Science from Stanford University. During their graduate studies, they conducted research with Professors Serena Yeung and Leonidas Guibas at the Stanford AI Lab.

researcher.name: Olivier Bousquet
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Director @ Google
researcher.bio: Olivier Bousquet co-developed Least-to-most prompting to enable complex reasoning in LLMs by decomposing problems into a sequence of simpler subtasks. He is a researcher at Google specializing in ML and learning theory. His earlier work includes Learning with local and global consistency, a semi-supervised method that propagates labels across data manifolds. Bousquet also authored Concentration inequalities for bounding empirical processes and co-created Wasserstein auto-encoders for generative modeling. Additionally, he helped develop Google research football, a multi-agent RL environment designed for testing decision-making agents. His broader research covers stability and generalization in algorithms and the use of Hilbert-Schmidt norms to measure statistical dependence.

researcher.name: Patrick von Platen
researcher.headline: Research Engineer @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Engineer @ Hugging Face
researcher.bio: Patrick von Platen's Transformers library provides a standardized interface for implementing and sharing NLP models. They are a Research Engineer at Mistral AI, where they focus on NLP and scalable systems. From 2019 to 2023, they worked as a Research Engineer at Hugging Face, creating Diffusers and serving as a core maintainer of Transformers. Their research includes the 176B-parameter multilingual model Bloom and recent Mistral architectures such as Magistral and Ministral 3. They also developed XLS-R for self-supervised cross-lingual speech representation learning and the distillation method Distil-whisper. They hold an MSc from RWTH Aachen University and were previously a PhD student at the University of Cambridge.

topAffiliation.description: Focused on natural language processing and scalable AI systems.

researcher.name: Paul Jacob
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Paul Jacob’s Pixtral 12B is a multimodal model that processes image and text data through a unified architecture. Jacob is a researcher at Mistral AI working on ML, CV, and deep learning. they are a contributor to the Magistral and Ministral 3 models, as well as the Voxtral series for speech and audio processing. Jacob’s research in medical AI includes Phikon-v2, a feature extractor for biomarker prediction, and methods for scaling self-supervised learning in histopathology using masked image modeling. They also developed Devstral for fine-tuning coding agents and STEEX for semantic counterfactual explanations. Their work further explores deep learning for cancer survival prediction and molecular subtype classification using histologic slides.

researcher.name: Paul Wambergue
researcher.headline: Research Engineer @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Paul Wambergue co-created Magistral, a language model developed at Mistral AI. As a researcher there, they focus on LLMs, coding agents, and audio-based architectures. Wambergue also co-authored Ministral 3 and the Voxtral series, which covers realtime audio and text-to-speech tasks. Their research on Devstral evaluates fine-tuning LLMs for coding agent applications. Wambergue's prior work includes the spectral analysis of MIXMAX random number generators and investigating how periodic sampling can improve model behavior in practice.

researcher.name: Pierre Stock
researcher.headline: VP Science @ Mistral, Previously Research Scientist @ Meta
researcher.bio: Pierre Stock co-developed Mistral 7B, a high-performance large language model designed for efficient inference. Currently at Mistral AI, they focus on ML and deep learning with an emphasis on model compression and architecture optimization. Stock also co-authored Mixtral of experts, which uses a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture to scale model capacity. In CV, Stock created LeViT, a vision transformer that incorporates convolutional elements for faster inference on hardware. Their research includes LLM-QAT for data-free quantization aware training and Pixtral 12B. Stock’s earlier work investigated differential privacy and federated learning, including methods for empirical privacy measurement through CANIFE.

topAffiliation.description: Drives model releases, roadmap strategy, and execution.

researcher.name: Piotr Miłoś
researcher.affiliation: Mistral AI|University of Warsaw, ex-(Google|visiting prof. U.Oxford)
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Associate Professor @ University of Warsaw, Associate Professor @ Institute of Mathematics, Polish Academy of Sciences
researcher.bio: Piotr Miłoś developed Model-based reinforcement learning for atari to enable sample-efficient agent training within learned world models. He is an AI Scientist at Mistral AI and an Associate Professor at the University of Warsaw. His research focuses on reasoning, RL, and LLMs, including the development of Moe-mamba for efficient selective state space models and Focused Transformer for context scaling. Miłoś also co-authored Thor to integrate LLMs with automated theorem provers and the robotic benchmark Continual World. He previously served as a Staff Software Engineer at Google and held a visiting professorship at the University of Oxford. He holds a PhD from the Institute of Mathematics of the Polish Academy of Sciences and has an academic background in probability theory and mathematical physics.

researcher.name: Poojan Shah
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral, Previously Undergraduate Student and Researcher @ IIT Delhi
researcher.bio: I’m an AI Scientist on the pretraining team at Mistral, where I work on making pretraining recipes for large transformers more efficient, stable, and predictable as they scale. I recently graduated from CSE @ IIT Delhi, where I worked with Ragesh Jaiswal on algorithms for clustering problems.

topAffiliation.description: Pretraining Science

researcher.name: Prateek Gupta
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Postdoctoral Researcher @ Max Planck Institute for Human Development
researcher.bio: Prateek Gupta co-created Oasis, an open-source framework for simulating social interactions among one million agents. Gupta is a Research Scientist at Mistral AI and a Postdoctoral Researcher at the Max Planck Institute for Human Development. Their research spans ML, RL, and combinatorial optimization, focusing on multi-agent systems and AI for science. Gupta also developed Hybrid models for learning to branch, which uses graph neural networks to improve decision-making in branch-and-bound solvers. Previously a visiting researcher at Mila and an intern at DeepMind, Gupta completed a PhD in ML at the University of Oxford and The Alan Turing Institute. They also investigate how LLMs influence human spoken communication and the emergence of cooperation in multi-agent systems.

researcher.name: Ram Ramrakhya
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously CS PhD Student @ Georgia Institute of Technology
researcher.bio: Ram Ramrakhya co-created GOAT-bench, a benchmark for evaluating multimodal lifelong navigation across diverse environments. They are a Research Scientist at Mistral AI and a PhD student at Georgia Tech focusing on RL and multimodal LLM agents. At Mistral, they develop infrastructure and interaction data for post-training agents, a focus informed by their work on the Habitat-matterport 3d semantics dataset. Their broader research includes the PARTNR benchmark for multi-agent tasks and the PIRLNav method for robot navigation. Ramrakhya previously interned at Apple, Meta, and AI2 and worked as a software engineer at Glance and InMobi. They are completing their PhD at Georgia Tech under the advisement of Dhruv Batra and Zsolt Kira.

topAffiliation.description: Works on scaling reinforcement learning infrastructure, interaction data, and environments for post-training multimodal LLM agents.

researcher.name: Remi Delacourt
researcher.headline: Research Engineer @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Remi Delacourt’s Magistral is a large language model. They are a researcher at Mistral AI working on LLM systems and inference efficiency. Delacourt developed FlexLLM to enable the concurrent serving of model inference and parameter-efficient fine-tuning. They also created AdaServe, a system that uses speculative decoding to optimize LLM serving for specific service-level objectives. Their additional work includes the language models Voxtral and Devstral, the latter of which is specialized for coding agent applications.

topAffiliation.description: Focuses on large-scale ML systems and LLM serving; helps design models under hardware and system constraints and improve their speed and efficiency.

researcher.name: Rishi Shah
researcher.affiliation: Masters in Machine Learning, Carnegie Mellon University
researcher.headline: AI Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously ML MSc Student @ Carnegie Mellon University
researcher.bio: Rishi Shah co-authored Dissecting Adversarial Robustness of Multimodal LM Agents, which analyzes attacks on vision-language model agents and introduces the Agent Robustness Evaluation framework. They are an AI Research Scientist at Mistral AI, after completing an MS in Machine Learning at Carnegie Mellon University, where they worked with Aditi Raghunathan on reasoning and adversarial robustness in multimodal agents. Their research focuses on robust multimodal AI, VLM reasoning, and AI systems. At Cartesia, they worked on distilling a multimodal TTS model into compact variants. Earlier, at Samsung Electronics, they developed generative AI and retrieval-augmented generation systems; they earned a BS in Computer Science from IIT Delhi.

researcher.name: Rohin Arora
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Mistral AI, Previously Video Engineering @ Apple
researcher.bio: Rohin Arora’s Voxtral realtime enables low-latency audio processing and generation for multimodal models. Arora is a researcher at Mistral AI where they focus on DL, CV, and audio synthesis. They also developed Voxtral tts to facilitate high-fidelity text-to-speech conversion. Previously, Arora authored Ai-enabling workloads on large-scale gpu-accelerated system, which characterizes performance bottlenecks and resource opportunities in AI supercomputing. Their earlier research at Northeastern University centered on improving resource utilization for GPU-accelerated hardware. Arora’s work focuses on the intersection of audio modeling and high-performance ML infrastructure.

topAffiliation.description: Contributed to the Voxtral Realtime and Voxtral TTS models.

researcher.name: Romain Sauvestre
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Engineer @ Meta
researcher.bio: Romain Sauvestre co-authored Llama 3, a suite of LLMs trained on massive datasets for reasoning and dialogue tasks. They are an ML researcher at Mistral AI, where they focus on the development of open-weight foundation models. Sauvestre contributed to Code Llama, which uses specialized fine-tuning to perform programming and infilling tasks. At Mistral AI, they worked on Pixtral 12B, a multimodal architecture that processes interleaved image and text sequences. Their research also includes Ministral 3 and the Voxtral series, addressing efficient model scaling and audio processing. Previously, Sauvestre applied CV techniques to medical imaging for fracture detection in musculoskeletal radiographs.

researcher.name: Roman Soletskyi
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Mistral AI, Previously Physics MSc Student @ Ecole Normale Supérieure – PSL
researcher.bio: Roman Soletskyi co-developed Pixtral 12B, a multimodal model that processes interleaved image and text inputs. Currently a researcher at Mistral AI, Soletskyi works on large-scale multimodal systems and LLM reasoning. They contributed to NuminaMath, a dataset of 860,000 competition-level math problems and solutions used for training mathematical AI. Their recent projects include Magistral and Ministral 3, as well as Voxtral for speech and audio tasks. Soletskyi also developed Combibench to benchmark LLM capabilities in combinatorial mathematics. Their broader research includes theoretical work on mode collapse in variational inference and incremental compression.

researcher.name: Rosalie Millner
researcher.headline: Researcher @ Mistral AI, MVA Student @ ENS Paris-Saclay
researcher.bio: Rosalie Millner’s Voxtral realtime enables low-latency, streaming audio processing for speech-to-speech interactions. They are a researcher at Mistral AI and affiliated with ENS-Paris Saclay and Dauphine-PSL. Their work focuses on multimodal ML, specifically speech synthesis and robotic control. Millner also developed Voxtral tts, a model designed for high-fidelity text-to-speech generation. With Robostral Navigate, they integrated vision-language models into autonomous navigation frameworks. This research targets the development of efficient LLM architectures capable of real-time performance in interactive and physical settings.

researcher.name: Sagar Vaze
researcher.affiliation: Mistral AI / VGG, University of Oxford
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Computer Vision and ML PhD Student @ University of Oxford
researcher.bio: Sagar Vaze co-developed SAM 3, which performs image segmentation by mapping visual regions to conceptual categories. Vaze is a Research Scientist at Mistral AI and a researcher at the University of Oxford VGG. Their research centers on CV and ML, specifically representation learning and multimodal LLMs. Vaze authored Open-set recognition, which uses closed-set classifiers to identify unknown categories, and Generalized category discovery, a framework for clustering images from both seen and unseen classes. They also contributed to the development of Pixtral 12B and Ministral 3. Vaze completed a PhD at Oxford and previously worked at Meta AI on the Segment Anything team.

topAffiliation.description: Working on multi-modal language models.

researcher.name: samuel humeau
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Lead ML @ Nabla
researcher.bio: Samuel Humeau’s Poly-encoders uses a hybrid Transformer architecture to speed up multi-sentence scoring tasks. He is a researcher at Facebook Research working on AI and NLP. His research focuses on conversational agents and multimodal systems, including Personalized Dialogue Agents designed for large-scale interactive use. Humeau also created Engaging Image Captioning, which incorporates personality traits into vision-to-language models. His work on model robustness includes Build it break it fix it, a framework for evaluating dialogue safety through adversarial human attacks. He has also investigated real-time inference strategies for deep pretrained models and multimodal attribute extraction.

researcher.name: Sanchit Gandhi
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Audio Team Lead @ Hugging Face
researcher.bio: Sanchit Gandhi co-authored Bloom, a 176-billion parameter open-access multilingual language model. They are a Research Scientist at Mistral AI specializing in LLMs and speech processing. Gandhi developed Distil-Whisper, which utilizes large-scale pseudo labeling to produce compressed, robust speech recognition models. Their work at Mistral AI includes the Magistral and Ministral 3 language models and the Voxtral suite for speech modeling and text-to-speech synthesis. Gandhi also contributed to the ESB multi-domain speech recognition benchmark and the Open ASR Leaderboard. They created RASMALAI to provide resources for adaptive speech modeling in Indian languages with various accents and intonations.

researcher.name: Sandeep Subramanian
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Manager @ NVIDIA
researcher.bio: Sandeep Subramanian co-authored Mixtral of experts, a sparse mixture-of-experts model that selectively activates parameter subsets for each token during inference. He is a researcher at Mistral AI focusing on DL and NLP. His recent work includes the multimodal architecture Pixtral 12B and the Magistral and Ministral 3 language models. Earlier, he developed Neural architectures for named entity recognition, which combines bidirectional LSTMs and conditional random fields for sequence tagging. Subramanian also contributed to Deep Complex Networks for complex-valued neural architectures and researched distributed sentence representations using multi-task learning.

topAffiliation.description: Focused on pretraining and advancing the capabilities of large language models.

researcher.name: Shashwat Verma
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Shashwat Verma’s Voxtral TTS provides a framework for real-time, high-fidelity speech synthesis. Verma is an AI researcher at Mistral AI specializing in LLMs, robotics, and efficient AI systems. They authored Voxtral realtime for low-latency audio generation and developed large-scale 3D visual instruction datasets to improve multimodal LLMs. Their research also explores training efficiency, including the use of the Muon optimizer to accelerate learning by preserving rare learning directions. Previously, Verma worked on autonomous vehicle navigation and published Context and intention aware planning for urban driving. They also hold patents for the automatic selection of compression artifact removal models.

researcher.name: Siddharth Gandhi
researcher.headline: Deep Learning @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Siddharth Gandhi’s Magistral is a large-scale language model architecture developed at Mistral AI. They are a researcher at Mistral AI specializing in ML, NLP, and information retrieval. Gandhi also co-authored Ministral 3, which focuses on performance in small-scale language models. Their research portfolio includes Voxtral for speech processing and Devstral, which fine-tunes models for use as coding agents. They also developed Unified multimodal discrete diffusion to handle diverse data types within a single generative framework. Prior to Mistral AI, Gandhi conducted research at the Technical University of Munich and Vellore Institute of Technology.

researcher.name: Simon Lepage
researcher.headline: Applied AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously PhD Student @ Criteo
researcher.bio: Simon Lepage's Voxtral TTS performs text-to-speech synthesis using a unified generative framework. They are a PhD student at École des Ponts ParisTech and a researcher at Mistral AI focusing on ML, deep learning, and retrieval. Lepage also developed Voxtral Realtime, which provides low-latency audio generation for interactive applications. In the domain of CV and retrieval, they created LRVS-Fashion, a dataset for visual search that uses natural language instructions to refine image similarity. Their work also includes Collaborative Tokenization, which improves the efficiency and accuracy of generative recommendation models.

researcher.name: Simon Sorg
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously CS MPhil Student @ University of Cambridge
researcher.bio: Simon Sorg co-developed Ministral 3, a model family designed for efficient, small-scale language processing. Sorg is a researcher at Mistral AI focusing on AI4Math and the Lean theorem prover. Their research investigates how LLMs handle symbolic and mathematical reasoning, as seen in Learning Modular Exponentiation with Transformers. They have also developed methods for translating informal mathematics into code, including Conjecture Extraction for Proof Autoformalization and Online Reinforcement Learning for Autoformalization. Beyond math, Sorg works on speech and audio systems such as Voxtral realtime and Voxtral tts.

researcher.name: Soham Ghosh
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ Google Deepmind
researcher.bio: Soham Ghosh co-developed Pixtral 12B, a multimodal model that combines vision-language understanding with text generation in a 12-billion parameter architecture. Currently a Research Scientist at Mistral AI, they work on multimodal LLMs, CV, and RL. Ghosh’s research includes Voxtral, a series of audio-chat models for speech and text processing, and VideoCoCa, which enables zero-shot video classification and retrieval. They also developed Tips to improve spatial reasoning in image-text models by blending contrastive learning with masked image modeling. Prior to Mistral AI, Ghosh was a researcher at Google DeepMind and earned an M.S. from Carnegie Mellon University. They completed their undergraduate studies at Nanyang Technological University.

topAffiliation.description: Works on open-source multimodal large language models such as Pixtral and Voxtral.

researcher.name: Szymon Antoniak
researcher.headline: AI Scientist @ Mistral AI
researcher.bio: Szymon Antoniak's Mixtral of experts employs a sparse mixture-of-experts architecture to scale LLM parameters while limiting active parameters during inference. Antoniak is a researcher at Mistral AI specializing in neural networks and AI. Their research focuses on architectural efficiency, including MoE-Mamba, which integrates mixture-of-experts with selective state space models. In the multimodal domain, Antoniak contributed to Pixtral 12B for vision-language tasks and the audio-focused Voxtral. They also investigated optimization strategies in Scaling laws for fine-grained mixture of experts. Recent work includes the development of the Magistral model and Devstral, a system for fine-tuning language models for coding agent applications.

researcher.name: Teven Le Scao
researcher.headline: Research Engineer, Reasoning @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Engineer @ Hugging Face
researcher.bio: Teven Le Scao co-authored Transformers, an open-source library for downloading and fine-tuning state-of-the-art NLP models. He is a Research Scientist at Hugging Face, focusing on LLM pretraining, scaling laws, and multilingualism. Le Scao was a primary developer of Bloom, a 176-billion-parameter multilingual model trained through the BigScience initiative. His work on T0 examined how multitask prompted training enables zero-shot generalization across diverse NLP tasks. More recently, he investigated Scaling Data-Constrained Language Models to determine the impact of training on repeated tokens when unique data is limited. He also co-developed Datasets, a community library for the efficient processing and sharing of NLP data.

topAffiliation.description: Worked on Magistral, Mistral's reasoning model and reinforcement-learning pipeline.

researcher.name: Théo Cachet
researcher.headline: Research Scientist @ Mistral AI, Previously Research Scientist @ NAVER LABS Europe
researcher.bio: Théo Cachet’s Ministral 3 provides high-performance language modeling optimized for edge computing. They are a Research Scientist at Mistral AI, specializing in ML, RL, and robotics. Cachet’s research includes Demonstration-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning, which enables agents to learn tasks from few-shot examples. They also developed Voxtral for real-time speech processing and Robostral for autonomous robotic navigation. Cachet completed a PhD at Sorbonne Université in 2025 for work on task generalization in multi-task RL.

researcher.name: Thibaut LAVRIL
researcher.headline: AI Research Engineer @ Mistral AI, Previously AI Research Engineer, FAIR @ Meta
researcher.bio: Thibaut Lavril co-authored Llama, a release of open foundation language models designed for high performance with reduced parameter counts. Now a researcher at Mistral AI, he specializes in LLM pre-training and efficient model architectures. He worked on Llama 2, which scaled the original framework and introduced fine-tuned models for chat applications. At Mistral, he contributed to Mistral 7B and Mixtral of experts, the latter of which uses sparse gating to improve computational efficiency.
